  the context-window RFC and RFC-AC-041 no longer describe the removed
  `input_policy` setting (#49239).
- Added the RFC `lane-addon-shutdown-detaches-native-instances`: a server that stops on SIGTERM or SIGINT detaches its own native Lane Add-on instances while its shutdown hooks run, so the next server attaches their declarations instead of waiting on another binary's cleanup descriptor (#49326)
- The multi-account plan sets the C2d scope: allowlist admission admits a Member, removing a registration writes an intent and registering does not, an invitation admission also spends the open registration of the identity, and C2d carries the Admin register and remove functions (#49353).
- The TOML reload matrix says runtime.toml model, provider, binding and lane rows need a server restart; only the `[fusion]` policy is read per request (#49362)
- RFC-provider-path-rest §3.3 says a rest without a stated time holds the
  walk order back only until its release, the 60-second floor for a 429 and
  the 900-second cap for a quota refusal, and records why the "until the next
  success" rule of RFC-0433 §3.1 is removed (#49388).
- RFC-0488 records the measurement after the live GLM rows kept prior reasoning: reasoning drops stopped and the GLM run first-request cache miss went from 49.8% to 27.8% (#49438)
- RFC-0491 records the first measurement after layer 4: every Keeper prompt captured after the deploy keeps the proof-pending mark out of System, and the phase-change cache measurement waits for a Goal event (#49440)
- The measured operator home RFC now asks for a captured TUI session as PR evidence, and limits tests to requests sent, state stored and decisions, as the constitution does (#49489)
- The TUI workbench RFC lists the six operator questions of the stats Goal with the server reads that already answer them, and cuts the planned `usage/series` read to tokens and cost because `tool-metrics/series` already gives tool calls, failures and p95 per hour or day (#49501)
- RFC-0486 states the shipped MSX·DOS observe-vs-control split — spectators only read frames `since` their last read and only the control screen advances the machine — and RFC-0480 points the closed stack PR numbers at their restacked landings in #48677 and #48678 (#49543).
- RFC-0493 is Implemented: every layer is merged, and after the 5d deploy a client reading the Observer stream stays connected for the full 120 s where it was dropped after 5 s (#49546)
- The multi-account plan sets the C3 scope: browser sessions are authorization records that end seven days after issue, a session is revoked through an intent, the session cookie and request checks, the login, logout, session, and Admin allowlist routes, and nine layers; WS/SSE session binding moves to C4 and route registration with the HTTP/2 arms to S1 (#49547).
- The TUI workbench RFC puts a 24 hour tool call line on the Dashboard first, because the turn series it asked for has no read yet and `tool-metrics/series` already holds the hourly calls and failures; the turn sparkline and the completed Task bars wait for `usage/series` (#49578)
- RFC-0510 proposes sending the second and later tool results of one turn whose text equals the first as a short stub that names the first result, switched per tool in TOML. `docs/evidence/repeated-tool-results-2026-11` holds the read-only script that measures those repeats in stored requests and in the tool-call ledger, its tests, and the results. It changes no server code (#49591).
- Research note for a Mistral Vibe official-client lane: the separate-pool reading of the Vibe Code console is a hypothesis requiring API/Vibe consumption-curve measurement against the official shared-usage documentation, the CLI's programmatic mode (`-p`, `--output json|streaming`, `export.json`, exit codes 0-3) is documented, and the first draft's "no headless" claim is corrected with the reason the sweep missed it (#49621).
- RFC draft for a Mistral Vibe official-client lane: command transport on the documented programmatic surface with masc owning the output codec (`--output json|streaming`, `export.json`, exit codes), a first-layer fixture-measured start condition, readiness-only credential posture, and measured-then-typed failure classification (#49622).
- The measurement script of RFC-0510 now also reports how far a same-turn repeated tool result sits from the first result with the same text, and RFC-0510 section 2.6 gives the numbers. It changes no server code (#49628).
- The TUI guide and the Keeper columns help sheet describe `NOW`, `AGE`, the unknown count and the failing group as the list computes them: `NOW` is read from turns, the waiting inventory, held calls, questions and async requests; `AGE` falls back to the start of a running turn that reports no update; a failing keeper counts under failing and not under unknown; a failed attempt does not move a paused or offline keeper into the failing group. It changes no server code (#49659).

### Internal

- The TUI Code diff overlay keys its fetched state by the comparison (`Diff_worktree` or `Diff_commit`) instead of the path, so a reply for one comparison of a file cannot land as another. A refresh keeps the comparison on screen. The git/diff read names exactly one of `base_ref` or `commit`. Nothing opens a commit diff yet (#48218).
- Remove nine exported functions that no code or test referenced, with their `.mli` declarations. (#48228)
- Add `Repo_git.grep_at`, a read-only fixed-string search over tracked and non-ignored files of a checkout, with literal pathspecs, at most 20 matches per file and a caller-set total. No match is an empty answer; a malformed or truncated `git grep` row is an error. Nothing calls it yet (#48229).
- TUI 가 `/api/v1/workspace/search` 응답을 읽는 `Tui_decode.decode_workspace_search` 와 `Masc_tui_http.fetch_workspace_search` 를 추가한다. 경로가 비었거나 줄 번호가 1 보다 작은 일치, `truncated` 가 없는 응답은 오류로 거절한다. 아직 호출하는 화면은 없다 (#48243).
- Make `Keeper_toml_loader` take `Keeper_toml_parser`'s types and functions with `include` instead of restating them, so `Keeper_toml_loader.toml_value` and `Keeper_toml_parser.toml_value` are the same type. (#48252)
- Make `keeper_types_profile_toml.mli` take `Keeper_types_profile_toml_io`'s interface with `include` instead of restating its 70 declarations. (#48258)
- Remove the unused `stop_group` helper chain (`stop_group`, `stopped`, `signal_group_id`, `await_empty`, `group_has_members`) from `Posix_spawn_detached`. (#48261)
- 체크아웃의 로컬 브랜치 목록을 읽는 `Repo_git.branches_at` 를 추가한다. 브랜치마다 이름, 현재 여부, upstream 대비 ahead/behind, 끝 커밋 시각과 제목을 한 번의 읽기 전용 `git for-each-ref` 로 읽는다. 읽을 수 없는 줄이나 ahead/behind 필드는 "동기 상태"로 읽지 않고 오류로 거절한다. 아직 부르는 곳은 없다 (#48262).
- Remove three exported functions that nothing calls: `Keeper_internal_error.fenced_cause_of_masc_internal_error`, `Exact_output_catalog_binding.target_positive_int_field` and `Execution_agent_scope.provider_request_provenance`. (#48263)
- Remove the unused `Tool_call_replay_harness` module (`lib/tool_surface/`), which nothing references since its test and fixtures were removed in #41034. (#48272)
- TUI 가 `/api/v1/git/branches` 응답을 읽는 `Tui_decode.decode_git_branches` 와 `Masc_tui_http.fetch_git_branches` 를 추가한다. 이름이 비었거나 시간이 음수인 브랜치, 정수가 아니거나 하나만 있는 ahead/behind 는 오류로 거절한다. 서버 라우트가 만든 JSON 을 이 디코더가 읽는지 왕복 시험으로 확인한다. 아직 호출하는 화면은 없다 (#48273).
- Remove four exported functions that nothing calls: `Env_config_memory.get_int_logged`, `Tool_usage_log.attach_source_metadata`, `Mcp_transport_protocol.request_meta_has_key` and `Lane_addon_store.binding_write_error_to_string`. (#48281)
- Remove three exported functions that nothing calls: `Lane_addon_store.tool_request_owner_inventory_all`, `Tool_args.get_string_required` and `Browser_stagehand_model.published_lane`. The contract text of the first moves into the doc of `fold_tool_request_owner_inventory_all`, and the stale "Production passes `published_lane`" sentence in `Browser_stagehand_model.create` is dropped. (#48284)
- Remove `Runtime_model_input_tail_window.project_target`, its `target_projection`, `target_fit` and `overrun_cause` types, the unused `target_fit_to_string` and the three tests that only exercised them. Nothing in production called them; the carried range uses `project_from_atom`. (#48286)
- Remove the unused `Types_core.tempo_mode` and `tempo_config` types, their eight conversion functions and the tests that only exercised them. The live `Tempo` module is a separate polling-interval reader and does not use them. (#48288)
- Narrow the interface of `Server_dashboard_http_composite_claims` to the values other modules use. (#48298)
- The Goal audit event ledger path is defined once in `Goal_store` and the dashboard Goal projections use it. (#48308)
- The local MASC server origin and the full health path each have one definition (`Masc_network_defaults.masc_http_loopback_origin` and `Server_health_paths.full`), and the server's upgrade preparation and runtime route use them. (#48310)
- The `masc` command line (restart, setup, owner upgrade, model resume and runtime config) builds the local server origin and the full health path from the same definitions as the server. (#48311)
- The environment variable names `MASC_BASE_PATH` and `MASC_CONFIG_DIR` come from `Env_config_core.base_path_env_key` and `Env_config_core.config_dir_env_key` in the workspace root, host config, config directory resolver, sandbox setup and server entry points. (#48314)
- The dashboard HTTP routes carry only the endpoints the dashboard calls, and an unknown dashboard path answers 404 in both the HTTP/1.1 router and the HTTP/2 gateway. (#48315)
- The raw trace record validator rejects every field outside its supported list with the same error, and its test uses an arbitrary unsupported field name. (#48316)
- Agent Core tests check unknown capability manifest keys once, in the manifest's own inline test, and test comments describe current behavior only. (#48318)
- Code comments describe current behavior only; comments that recorded removed code are dropped or rewritten as the rule that still applies. (#48321)
- `Keeper_gate` takes the 22 declarations it shared with `Keeper_gate_types`
  through `include module type of struct include Keeper_gate_types end`
  instead of restating them. Twelve of the restated types were separate types
  from the `Keeper_gate_types` ones and are now equal to them. The doc comments
  that only the facade carried moved into `keeper_gate_types.mli` (#48325).
- `Dashboard_goals_types` takes the declarations of its four layers (accessor,
  health, timeline, builder) through `include module type of struct include ...
  end` instead of restating 42 of them. `tree_node`, `goal_detail_keeper` and
  `build_context` are now equal to the layers' types. The doc comments that only
  the facade carried moved into the layer interfaces (#48328).
- The module headers of `Dashboard_goals_types` and its four layers describe
  what each module holds and depends on, and no longer tell how the module was
  split out (#48330).
- The event-queue operator, memory cleanup, shutdown reconciliation and HITL
  recover dashboard handlers take the Keeper API path prefix from
  `Server_dashboard_http_keeper_api_types.keeper_api_prefix` instead of each
  spelling it (#48338).
- The Goals dashboard facade exposes its `tree_node` record as the same type as
  the one in the Goals types module, so values of either type are accepted
  where the other is expected (#48346).
- Async request records and the async request projection pass JSON field lists
  to the code that adds fields of its own, instead of a JSON object that the
  caller takes apart again (#48352).
- Skill observability profiles expose their field list, so the effective tool
  surface and the skill snapshot route add or drop fields without taking the
  JSON object apart again (#48353).
- Closing a board post checks its successor in the same match as the post
  lookup, and tests cover refusing a post that names itself or a missing post
  as its successor (#48356).
- `lib/board` and `lib/task` build with warning 4 (fragile match) as an error, like the other libraries under `lib/`. `Task_history_page.cursor_of_string` matches the decoded `ceilings` first and the cursor fields second, and has direct tests for the tokens it accepts and refuses (#48360).
- The Lane Add-on web-search port reads the typed answer that the provider chain and the cache produce, instead of splitting provider error strings and re-reading cached tool JSON. Tool output is unchanged. The add-on runner has tests for cache-hit parity and the grounded serving provider (#48363).
- `Keeper_prompt` opens each helper module once (#48379).
- Subscription read and acknowledge share one reader that takes the fields it accepts and how the request carries a receipt, so no match needs an unreachable branch (#48380).
- Dashboard comments and test fixtures no longer cite a server route and an environment variable that do not exist (#48381).
- Four exports with no callers are removed: `Candidate_fault.of_transport_error` with its
  `dispatch` type, `Keeper_turn_boundaries.states_position` and
  `Runtime_muse_msp.turn_interrupt_request`. The tool help registry no longer carries a
  tool-family classifier that matched no tool, and its interface header describes how an
  entry is built from a tool's `[help]` table or its schema (#48396).
- The dashboard connector view reads connector ids, display names and state
  labels from `connector-constants.ts`, `connector-state.ts` and
  `config/connector-ids.ts` directly, and `connector-status.ts` no longer
  re-exports them. The activation text lookup returns `null` for an id the
  dashboard does not know instead of casting (#48399).
- Dashboard comments and test names describe connectors as they work today
  instead of sidecars, Start All toasts and sidecar status files (#48403).
- The benchmark bootstrap, the eval harnesses and the observation probe no
  longer export environment variables the server does not read, and the
  duplicated autonomous-flag export in two harnesses is gone (#48406).
- Keeper memory comments state what the librarian answer carries and what
  apply does today (#48407).
- The memory search index takes one row filter per query: every row, or every
  row except one owner's, cut to a result limit. The owner and the limit travel
  together (#48410).
- The MCP server and its HTTP transport share one `tool_profile` type, so the
  transport hands a profile to the server as it is instead of converting it
  constructor by constructor in three places (#48412).
- The MCP tool profile names (`full`, `managed_agent`, `operator_remote`,
  `seat`) are written once next to the profile type, for telemetry, error
  messages and the persisted session file (#48413).
- Redaction of URL userinfo lives in one string utility module, shared by the
  runtime config reader, the web search setup and the Keeper environment
  scrub (#48429).
- Substring search in the config snapshot, IDE memo, vision artifact scan,
  Slack poll and gateway, multimodal routes and input, wiki links, web search,
  exec log sanitizer and internal error classifier calls the shared string
  utility instead of a private loop (#48432).
- The string utility library gains a last-occurrence substring search, used by
  the repository pull-request client and the local runtime HTTP probe to split
  curl output at its status trailer (#48435).
- Prefix checks in fifteen modules use `String.starts_with` instead of cutting
  a substring first, and three private prefix helpers are gone (#48447).
- Suffix checks in the MSX tools, dashboard keeper API, repositories route and
  web fetch use `String.ends_with`, and helpers that only repeated the standard
  `starts_with` or `ends_with` are gone (#48448).
- `Llm_provider.Types.api_response` carries `unreadable_tool_uses`: tool calls with an id and a name whose argument text is not one JSON object, with that text, the parse problem and how a stream assembled it. Every producer leaves it empty in this change. The response cache stores it (schema 3 to 4, so older entries are misses), and the provider response snapshot of the execution journal refuses a response that still carries one (#48458).
- 저장소의 worktree 목록을 읽는 `Repo_git.worktrees_at` 를 추가한다. 항목마다 디렉터리의 마지막 이름, 체크아웃 상태(브랜치·detached·bare), 전체 HEAD, 잠김·정리 대상(prunable) 여부를 한 번의 읽기 전용 `git worktree list --porcelain -z` 로 읽는다. 절대 경로는 담지 않는다. 읽을 수 없는 레코드는 건너뛰지 않고 오류로 거절한다. 아직 부르는 곳은 없다 (#48463).
- Embedded tool definitions are looked up by name in one module,
  `Tool_definition_embedded`, instead of by a copy in each schema module. The
  `lib/tool_surface` shard modules use it (#48464).
- The `lib/tool_schemas` modules read their embedded tool definitions through
  `Tool_definition_embedded`, and the library no longer depends on
  `embedded_config` (#48465).
- The Task, Keeper, Operator, Board, agent-core projection, DOS and MSX schema
  readers use `Tool_definition_embedded`, so only that module spells the
  `tools/<name>.toml` path. A missing DOS or MSX tool definition is reported as
  `embedded tool definition missing: tools/<name>.toml` (#48466).
- 디렉터리가 속한 저장소의 worktree 목록을 주는 `GET /api/v1/git/worktrees?path=` 를 추가한다. 체크아웃을 찾는 방식은 브랜치 목록과 같고, 답은 `{root, worktrees, truncated}` 이다. worktree 마다 디렉터리의 마지막 이름, main 여부, 전체 HEAD, 상태(`branch`·`detached`·`bare`)와 브랜치, 잠김·정리 대상 여부를 담는다. 호스트의 절대 경로는 답에 없다. 최대 500개이고 넘으면 `truncated` 가 `true` 이다. 아직 TUI 는 부르지 않는다 (#48470).
- Month directories of the event log are ordered by one function,
  `Dated_jsonl.Layout.compare_month_entries`, which the event readers share
  instead of each carrying a copy (#48471).
- The dashboard runtime diagnostics report an `agent_state` entry only for the
  log phrase that the workspace and gRPC heartbeat code write when an agent
  record fails to decode (#48473).
- `Authz_bootstrap` writes the first authorization record through
  `Authz_zone.install`, the same steps as a zone commit: it runs
  `Authz_state.apply` before the append and confirms the end of the log before
  it gives up the intent of an earlier bootstrap, so an intent whose record
  reached the log after the checks is left for the next boot to promote
  (#48474).
- `/api/v1/git/worktrees` 의 답을 읽는 `Tui_decode.decode_git_worktrees` 와 요청 함수 `Masc_tui_http.fetch_git_worktrees` 를 추가한다. 상태 이름과 브랜치 칸이 맞지 않는 줄, bare 가 아닌데 HEAD 가 없는 줄, 모르는 상태, 빈 이름은 오류로 거절한다. 아직 부르는 곳은 없다 (#48476).
- The JSON redaction pass for secret-bearing keys lives in one function,
  `Secret_patterns.redact_json_with`, which the log sink and the observability
  previews both call (#48478).
- The tool definition and MCP surface decoders read TOML values through one
  module, `Toml_access`, so the "must be a <kind>, got <found>" messages have a
  single source (#48480).
- Keeper secret redaction derives the exact value it masks from
  `Keeper_secret_projection.strip_one_final_newline`, the same function that
  reads env secrets for projection (#48484).
- The OpenAI Responses backend and the tool-result projection check for an
  image block in tool results through `Types.content_has_image` (#48488).
- Code 화면이 언어 서버에게 파일 개요(`textDocument/documentSymbol`)와 진단(`textDocument/publishDiagnostics` 의 내용)을 읽기 전용으로 묻는 안을 RFC 로 적는다. `ocamllsp 1.27.0` 으로 잰 시간과 크기, 편집기가 이미 한다는 반론, 구현 전에 정해야 할 다섯 가지를 담는다. 코드는 바꾸지 않는다 (#48490).
- Keeper Memory program and message-floor validation, and the unread-message
  set, share one source key and one source digest from
  `Keeper_librarian_unread` (#48494).
- The plan error projection encodes export resolution errors next to the other
  plan errors. Composition results, nested-run evidence and the composition
  projection call it directly. (#48498)
- Workspace memory modules share one order and one map for fact references.
  The ledger exports them, and the ledger view, the Curator request and the
  Curator decision use them. (#48499)
- The official-client runtime modules share one turn image type and one turn
  image check, next to the media type set and the Base64 rule they read.
  (#48502)
- Muse serve and Fusion take the same turn image type as the other
  official-client runtimes, and Muse serve checks each image with the shared
  media type and Base64 rules. (#48504)
- `docs/evidence/tool-result-carry-2026-11/measure_tool_result_carry.py` counts the
  tool-result bytes that stored requests carry, by tool, and splits out the blob
  stubs and the stored-only `text_content` copies. Over 2026-10-29 to 11-04 the
  tool results are 3.996 GB of carried bytes, `masc_dos_*` results are 42.8% of
  it, and 16 of their 4,804 results are stubs. RFC-0363 §3.1.1 records why results
  that arrive as typed blocks have no demotion path and what a fix has to change
  first (#48506).
  `measure_dos_screen_trim.py` in the same directory replays a trim of the
  DOS `screen_text` page, 25 rows of 80 columns padded with spaces, over the
  stored requests. All 4,764 pages in that window are blank, the trim removes
  nothing but spaces and newlines, and it would have saved 265.6 MB, 2.30% of
  the request bodies (#48506).
- The Codex, Claude Code and Muse Keeper runtimes hand a goal's images to their
  clients as the shared official-client turn image type, with no per-runtime
  copy. (#48513)
- `List_util` has `strip_prefix` and `is_prefix`. The history checks of the
  direct continuations, history clear, wait response, input checkpoint, journal
  preparation, history cut and native result retention call them. (#48515)
- The path and segment prefix checks of the owned job volumes, the official
  client context, the alerting path, the sandbox location, the shell tool
  command table, the account removal, the keeper TOML loader and the dashboard
  runtime info call `List_util.is_prefix` and `List_util.strip_prefix`. (#48517)
- The prefix checks of the exec policy script paths, the chat operation store
  batches and the librarian counterpart snapshots call `List_util.is_prefix` and
  `List_util.strip_prefix`. (#48522)
- The workspace query, the telemetry store and the dashboard bridge call the
  standard `List.take` directly. (#48525)
- The keeper world observation message scope calls `List_util.take_last`.
  (#48526)
- The exact lane, goal verification, fusion and verification run registries
  return the install result of the run registry core as it is from
  `install_global`. (#48529)
- `Fs_compat` keeps one append-only line fold, and its interface documents
  that fold next to its value. (#48532)
- `Agent_observation` exposes only the attribution and annotation
  vocabulary, and Keeper tool executions keep no event list in server
  memory. (#48535)
- Server startup keeps no process-wide copy of the config journal recovery
  report, and the Skill catalog snapshot service refreshes through a single
  path. (#48538)
- `scripts/harness/perf/tui_request_proxy.py` relays HTTP/1.1 between local
  clients and one server and logs, per exchange, the method, path, query names,
  final status, each server-sent event by name, how the exchange ended and the
  bytes each side took. It stores no header values, query values or bodies
  (#48539).
- `scripts/harness/perf/tui_request_probe.py` starts one TUI binary with its
  `--port` set to the relay from #48539 and reports, per step window, the
  requests that started in it and the server-sent events that arrived in it,
  so two TUI binaries can be compared against the same server (#48540).
- Seven small modules no longer export forwarding wrappers next to the
  functions they forward to. (#48542)
- The metric store's lock failure path logs the caller stack and keeps no
  second copy of it in memory. (#48543)
- Keeper, runtime model, TypeSafe AI and lane add-on modules no longer export
  seven conversion and summary helpers that no code calls. (#48545)
- The workspace state record drops three fields that were set at bootstrap
  and read by no code. (#48548)
- With `MASC_TUI_FRAME_TIMING` set, the TUI's frame-timing report also lists
  the surface each frame it wrote showed, as runs keyed by the ordinal of the
  run's first written frame, and the number of frames it wrote (#48561).
- `scripts/harness/perf/tui_request_probe.py` reports, per step window, the
  TUI surfaces on screen in it. It counts the frames the terminal received
  and reads each one's surface from the TUI's surface runs (#48561), and names
  none when the two counts differ (#48562).
- The autonomous phase library and its two tests are removed. The library
  held a fixed list of phase and transition names that no module referenced
  once its HTTP routes were gone. (#48566)
- The two TLA+ specs for the autonomous phase taxonomy and its tick, and the
  lines that ran them in `scripts/tla-check.sh`, are removed. Their OCaml
  counterpart no longer exists. (#48568)
- Keeper turns no longer run the two multimodal post-turn passes or copy tool
  results into the per-keeper accumulator that fed them. No tool emitted the
  marker keys, so the passes only rewrote a checkpoint copy that nothing read
  (#48579).
- Remove the multimodal artifact workspace modules (`Artifact`, `Payload`,
  `Workspace`, `Workspace_holder`, `Keeper_emitter`, `Multimodal_hydrator`,
  `Multimodal_keeper_bridge`, `Tool_emission`, `Wirein_helpers`) and their
  tests. `lib/multimodal` keeps the `Vision_*` modules (#48589).
- Remove the TLA+ specs `MultimodalArtifact` and `MultimodalHydrator` and the
  `scripts/tla-check.sh` lines that run them, and regenerate `specs/INDEX.md`
  (#48590).
- Remove `Jsonl_incremental_projection` and its two tests; the keeper decision
  feed it served is gone (#48594).
- Comments in `lib/keeper` state what the code does now instead of retelling
  removed features (#48601).
- Comments outside `lib/keeper` state what the code does now instead of
  retelling removed features (#48602).
- Test comments in `packages/agent_core` state what each test checks instead
  of retelling removed code (#48603).
- The plain Dashboard layout draws its Action needed block from one list of rows (the heading, the reasons and the `+N more` row), so the height it reserves is the height it draws. The screen does not change (#48605).

The Keeper tool approval answer and the composer release travel in `keeper_msg` as `Keeper_tool_approval_answered` and `Keeper_composer_released`.

- The authorization log has an `invite` record kind whose body is an issued or a revoked invitation, with the SHA-256 of the token in place of the token. No layer reads it yet, so the state refuses it (#48682).
- The TUI's Code answers are declared in `Masc_tui_code_results` next to the functions that apply them. Its `apply` returns what is left for the event loop, and the protocol and the loop decide by `answer_kind` instead of listing every Code answer. Code requests deliver only Code answers, and `masc_tui.ml` wraps them in `Code_msg` in one place, `deliver_code`. It stamps a read with the workspace that asked when the request starts, and sends the draft save unstamped (#48685, #48664).
- Four more modules call the shared JSON field reader instead of private
  copies, and `Keeper_reaction_ledger_wire` no longer exports its copy (#48686).
- The authorization state reads invite records: the local operator issues Admin invitations and revokes them, an invite id and a token digest name one invitation for good, and the writer zone appends the issue of an invitation with no intent in the external store, after it settles what an earlier commit left. A revocation is a `revoke` intent on the invitation, so a log restored from before it does not match the store (#48692).
- The authorization log has an `admission` record kind: one record names the new user id, the external identity it binds (a Google `sub` or a GitHub user id), and the invitation it spends. No layer reads it yet, so the state refuses it (#48697).
- The authorization state reads admission records: one record spends an open invitation before its expiry, binds a Google or GitHub identity, and makes a principal, and an Admin invitation makes the person an Admin with a `grant` intent in the external store. Only the person who joins writes it, and a spent invitation, a user id given before, or an identity bound before is refused. A revocation of an invitation that the store gave up blocks that invitation from the record after its intent on, also when the commit that gave it up fails later, and a start keeps the block (#48701).
- The authorization log has an `admin_assignment` record kind: the revocation of the Admin assignment of a principal, with a required cause (`security_incident` or `operational`). An authenticated principal writes it. No layer reads it yet, so the state refuses it (#48704).
- The authorization state reads Admin assignment records: an Admin issues invitations of either role and revokes any invitation, and revokes the Admin assignment of another Admin or their own while another Admin remains. The last Admin assignment is never revoked, and an Admin whose revocation the store gave up writes nothing and does not count as the one that remains. A revocation is a `revoke` intent on the principal in the external store (#48711).
- With `MASC_TUI_NAV_TRACE` set to a file, the TUI appends one JSON line for each screen it opens and for each key after which the frame stayed the same: the key's name, whether the footer announced it, and never the text of a draft. A run writes up to 4096 lines (#48719).
- An admission record also makes the person a member of the workspace of the installation, with an account home namespace of their own. An admission that names another workspace, or a namespace given before, is refused. A namespace has no capital letter, because two names that differ only in case would name one directory on a file system that does not tell case apart (#48720).
- The authorization log reads the body of a `principal` record: a human principal disabled, enabled again, or deleted, the deletion carrying the identity it was bound to. No layer reads the record yet, so the state refuses it (#48720).
- The TUI's Context inspector answers are declared in a new `Masc_tui_context_results` library next to the function that applies them. The protocol and the loop decide by `answer_kind` instead of listing the answers, and `masc_tui.ml` wraps them in `Context_msg` in one place, `deliver_context`, which stamps them when the request starts (#48721, #48664).

- The authorization state reads `principal` records: an Admin that acts disables, enables again, or deletes a human principal. A disable is a `disable` intent and a deletion a `delete` intent in the external store, and an enable has none. A deletion frees the identity for a new principal and keeps the user id and the namespace given. A disabled or deleted principal writes nothing, and the last Admin check counts only Admins that are active and not blocked (#48741).

- The authorization zone reads its clock inside its locks for the time of each record, so a caller can no longer bring a time read before it waited for the lock. The authorization state keeps the latest time it has read and refuses an admission before it (`Admission_behind_log`), so a clock set back cannot spend an invitation that had expired by the time of a record already in the log. Other kinds are not held to that time. A draft no longer carries a time, and `Authz_bootstrap` takes the clock in its request (#48770).

Over 2026-11-01 to 11-05 it finds 60 shutdowns, 62 cut turns and 21 repeat cuts of 8 turns. Of 17 resumed turns that had grown their context before the stop, 15 carry at least 80 percent of that growth into the first request after it. 12 of 959 later calls repeat an earlier call. - `Oidc_google.identity` reads the Google identity of an ID token whose signature C1 checked: `iss` must be one of the two values Google documents, `aud` one string equal to the client ID (a list is refused), the nonce that of the login, and `sub` a Google subject; nothing calls it yet (#49197).
- `Oidc_login_transaction` keeps a login in flight under a random ID with its state, nonce, and PKCE verifier, gives it back once with its state before ten minutes pass, refuses a start when full of live logins, holds an invitation token that only its digest leaves, and parses `return_to` as an RFC 3986 path; nothing calls it yet (#49198).
- `Oidc_google_exchange` turns the code of a Google callback into the identity its ID token names: endpoints from the discovery document, the token exchange with the PKCE verifier, the JWKS kept for its `Cache-Control` max-age and read once more on an unknown key ID, then the signature and claim checks; the transport is a function and nothing calls it yet (#49199).

- `Authz_principal_state` keeps the external identities of deleted principals, read from the `Deleted` events of `authz.jsonl` and stored in no principal record, and `was_deleted` answers whether a deleted principal used an identity (#49210).
- `Authz_login.sign_in` decides a login once its Google identity is checked: a bound active principal signs in, a disabled, blocked or uncertain one is refused, and an unbound identity with an invitation token joins through one admission record that spends the invitation and binds the identity, with the user id redrawn when taken and a concurrent second admission refused as a conflict; nothing calls it yet (#49211).
- RFC-0493 now has the MCP GET, AG-UI and presence drains write queued frames in one send (layer 5d), after reading masc-tui clients were disconnected 579 times in six hours by a drain that waited once per frame (#49213)

- `Google_login_flow` runs a Google login from its start to the admission: the client from `auth_config.google` and its secret variable, a start that holds no transaction when Google cannot be read, and a callback that spends its transaction first; `Oidc_google_exchange.Client.make` refuses an empty ID or secret and a redirect URI that is not https, and nothing calls the flow yet (#49231).

Removing an entry will be a `Revoke` of it, so a restore that rewinds the removal does not let the identity in again. The design names the subject in §4.5 and its intent in §8.2 (#49377).

No state reads it yet (#49384).
- The authorization state reads `registration` records. A registration writes no intent; a removal writes a `Revoke` of the registration, so a restored log does not reopen it. The Admin who wrote a registration does not lift the block of its given-up removal; another Admin does. The cancel refusal `Canceller_issued_the_invitation` is now `Canceller_owns_the_subject` (#49385).

## [0.68.0] - 2026-11-05

### Upgrade notes

- Update Dashboard and TUI clients with the server for the `inspect_path`, `nonregular` and `mirror_nonregular` tokens. Older binaries cannot decode new values recorded in Goal verification, Keeper turn-boundary or dependent Librarian evidence; review “Goal store path failures and rollback” in `docs/guides/DURABLE-STORE-HARD-CUT.md` before rolling back (#47613).
- Docker, Kata and SSH Keeper proof scripts require a pinned `masc` binary
  with `inspect-checkpoint`; an older binary is refused before the Keeper
  workflow starts. (#47665)
- Every boot now reads the install record under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/masc` (or `~/.config/masc`), so a boot is refused when that directory exists and its group or others can write it; masc creates it with mode 0700, and `chmod 700` on it clears the refusal (#48196).
- A relative `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is now ignored when masc looks for its config directory, and `~/.config/masc` is used instead, as the XDG Base Directory Specification asks; the default base path record and the install record are both read from that one directory. `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `HOME` are trimmed of surrounding white space for both, so `" /cfg "` names `/cfg` (#48206).
- Keeper turns no longer write `<base>/.masc/keeper-wake-payload`, and startup pruning no longer looks at it. Nothing reads that folder, so an operator can delete it. (#48373)

### Fresh state required

- Operator apps move to `.masc/identity/apps/<client_group>.json`; enter them
  again with `A` on the Identity tab or `POST /api/v1/keepers/oauth/client`.
  The old `.masc/identity/<client_group>/` files are not read. A Keeper
  attached before this change has no record of its login's client, so its
  next renewal asks it to be attached again. (#47658)
- Keeper turn records and official-client sessions that name the `admitted_scheduled_input` prompt block are not read, and the deploy preflight refuses the install while a turn record names it. Stop the server, delete `<base-path>/.masc/keepers/*/turn-records` and every official-client `session.json` that names the block, then install (#47806).
- Keeper event queues use state schema `keeper.event_queue.state.v21` and the
  WAL `event-queue-transitions-v10.jsonl`. Stop the server, delete
  `<base-path>/.masc/keepers/*/event-queue-v19.json` and
  `<base-path>/.masc/keepers/*/event-queue-transitions-v9.jsonl`, then install
  (#47996).
- Board attention candidate ledgers use `schema_version` 8, and the deploy
  preflight refuses a ledger with any other version. A partition names its
  candidates by id, so with the server stopped delete both
  `<base-path>/.masc/board_attention_candidates/` and
  `<base-path>/.masc/board_attention_partitions/`, then install (#47996).
- A paused-work disposition receipt whose `source` is a Board stimulus without
  `audience` is not read, and the deploy preflight refuses the install while
  one exists. Delete the file the refusal names
  (`<base-path>/.masc/paused-work-dispositions-v7/keeper-*/operation-*.json`),
  then install (#47996).
- A Muse Keeper's `official-client-runtime/session.json` written by an earlier build is not read: stop the server, delete `<base>/.masc/keepers/<Muse Keeper>/official-client-runtime/session.json`, and install (#48054).
- Official-client sessions that hold the `repository_freshness` context
  section are not read, and the deploy preflight and boot refuse while one
  remains. Stop the server, delete every official-client `session.json` that
  holds the section, then install (#48074).
- Delete `.masc/lane-addons/ego-input` before starting this version. (#48102)

### Added

- Record a per-workspace claim on an Apple keeper's work volume. Dissolution
  releases its claim and always keeps the work and build volumes: the last
  recorded claim plus an empty owner listing cannot prove that no legacy,
  adopted, or paused-unrecorded owner in another workspace needs them.
  Fresh Apple provisioning stops if the claim helper fails or returns an
  unexpected report. Dissolution refuses single-line release reports with
  extra output (#47267, issue #47237).
- Refuse claims markers outside the supported line format before adding or
  releasing a claim. The helper requires `cmp` to detect changed bytes,
  including embedded NULs, and refuses if that check is unavailable (#47267).
- Refuse malformed or contradictory Apple volume inventory rows rather than
  treating an unidentified volume as absent (#47267).
- Add the `masc_sandbox_volume_gc` admin tool: it reports retired keepers'
  Apple work and build volumes with a per-keeper reason (a container still
  referencing the keeper, remaining claims-marker claimants, a local
  registration), and with `execute` can reclaim build-only volumes with no
  observed reference. Missing or empty markers keep work volumes because they cannot
  exclude unrecorded owners; unreadable listings, markers, or a run without
  an image also keep the affected volumes. A delete re-reads the inventory
  at delete time and preserves a keeper whose shape changed, and past that
  confirmation the platform's refusal to delete a referenced volume plus
  the absence check settle the removal (#47276, issue #47237).
- Add an offline Board posts inspection and explicit bootstrap/adoption library. Bind operator intent to physical workspace identity and complete raw content; preserve actual posts and guard publication receipts, uncertainty and reserved settlement exceptions. Live startup guard enforcement remains separate. (#47302)
- Add `workspace-upgrade board-posts inspect`, `bootstrap` and `adopt`. Mutations require an explicit root/content intent and the configured host BasePath lease, with structured publication outcomes and attempted lease release. Inspection creates no files or lease. (#47303)
- Preview remote images with colour cells when the terminal cannot display native graphics. (#47569)
- The Keeper Turn Inspector has an **입력과 실행** tab linking the selected turn's intake, runtime choices, prompt views, Skill calls and tool results. Missing records, repeated attempts and incomplete scans remain visible. Skill observations retain their original trace scope and distinguish physical async actions from causal links. Guide: docs/KEEPER-USER-MANUAL.md, "Follow an input through a turn" (#47625).
- Query Skill activity by the exact receiving Keeper turn across retained origin traces. The read-only projection keeps original activation frames, ledger revisions, physical result handoffs, causal actions and incomplete-read diagnostics together. Guide: docs/KEEPER-USER-MANUAL.md, "Follow an input through a turn" (#47639).
- The Keeper Identity tab shows the OAuth callback the server would send
  providers to, following `MASC_HTTP_BASE_URL` or the bound address, and
  marks services with an operator app on file. Pending-login prompt rows are
  now counted when the tab scrolls to the cursor row
  ([usage guide](https://github.com/jeong-sik/masc/blob/main/docs/KEEPER-IDENTITY-MANUAL.md)) (#47659).
- `masc inspect-checkpoint --base-path PATH --keeper NAME` prints a decoded
  canonical checkpoint and its closed-message boundary. Its output can contain
  conversation context and tool results. See the [SSH Keeper proof guide](docs/evidence/2026-10-24-remote-ssh-keeper/README.md). (#47665)
- Turn Inspector joins queue outcomes to exact turn-entry source snapshots and admission revisions, preserving failed attempts, partial reads and unresolved receipts. Guide: `docs/KEEPER-USER-MANUAL.md`, "Follow an input through a turn" (#47674).
- Report a refused ego task space in the browser lane connection inventory as an `ego_user_owned_space` issue with the Space name, its user-owned ids and the observation time, instead of a silent empty client list. (#47695)
- Reclaim an ego task space whose task ended while the operator held it with `take_over` on the live lane without a client id: the worker claims the space through the SDK claim call and reconnects without a restart, answering with a `reclaimed` receipt. (#47696)
- Support generation-bound SSE Observer delivery and replay. (#47722)
- The Keeper question log announces `keeper_asks_changed` and the Lane Add-on installation question log announces `lane_addon_asks_changed` after each recorded question, answer or withdrawal (#47748).
- A Keeper's durable async message request store announces `keeper_async_requests_changed` after a request record is written, removed from the active inventory, or rolled back (#47751).
- The pending confirmation store announces `pending_confirms_changed` after a write that changes what readers list, and the expiry worker announces when a confirmation passes its deadline or when its deadline read recovers from a failure. Removing confirmations past their deadline on a read is not announced (#47759).
- A schedule store write drops the cached fleet schedule list and is announced as `schedules_changed` from a separate fiber, so the store's writer does no network fanout (#47761).
- Administrator gate roster answers carry `candle_decay`, the Candle fold before decay to the read time; `Candle_decay_basis` computes balances and supply from it at any later time (#47880).
- The server announces `keeper_turn_changed` to one workspace's observers after a Keeper's turn slot, autonomous turn ref, chat control token, shutdown operation id or Owner availability changes (#47893).
- The server announces `keeper_turn_preview_changed` to one workspace's observers after a write to the preview the turns answer shows, sending a burst once per `post_interval_s` (#47900).
- The verification request store announces `workspace_dataset_changed` with `dataset` `verification_requests` to its workspace's observers after it writes or removes a request (#47908).
- The server announces `workspace_dataset_changed` with `dataset` `repositories` to a workspace's observers after a repository catalog write (#47917).
- A microVM keeper's TOML can set `microvm_delivery = "agent_socket"`
  (default `exec_per_request`; Apple `container` only). Its guest then boots
  with the shim's agent as the first process and publishes the agent's
  socket at `<base>/.masc/microvm/agent/`. Requests still use an exec per
  request until the next layer connects to the agent. Guide:
  `docs/KEEPER-USER-MANUAL.md`, "One isolated Apple microVM Keeper" (#47919).
- The server announces `keeper_event_queue_changed` (with `keeper`) to the workspace after a Keeper's event queue or reaction record is written, and drops the cached fleet schedule list first (#47934).
- A keeper with `microvm_delivery = "agent_socket"` now sends its requests
  through the guest agent's socket instead of one `container exec` per
  request. Before an agent guest that matches its plan is adopted, one probe
  goes through the socket; a guest whose agent does not answer is replaced.
  Guide: `docs/KEEPER-USER-MANUAL.md`, "One isolated Apple microVM Keeper"
  (#47939).
- TUI Tools screen deletes a published Skill with a double `d` press, reading
  the current reference first and showing the recovery receipt (originally
  #47862, fragment missing; usage guide: `docs/SKILLS-FLOW.md`) (#47968).
- `Keeper_types_support.append_keeper_metrics` announces `keeper_metrics_appended` with the Keeper's name to the workspace's observers after each metrics row is written (#48002).
- A committed runtime.toml text announces `runtime_config_changed` to the workspace's observers once it is visible on disk; catalogue publications that write no text announce nothing (#48036).
- `MASC_TUI_ALLOC_PROFILE=<file>` samples where the TUI's UI domain allocates and appends the allocation sites, ranked by estimated words, to that file at exit. 가이드 없음(docs/evidence/tui-keeper-list-held-key-20261104/alloc/README.md) (#48056).
- Each published skill catalog snapshot drops the full-health snapshot and announces `skill_catalog_published` to the workspace's observers (#48059).
- A lane add-on that exports tools announces `lane_addon_exports_changed` to the workspace's observer sessions whenever its exports move, beside the owner event and the MCP `tools/list_changed` (#48060).
- The server announces `gate_connector_changed {connector}` to runtime observers, one per changed connector from a batching fiber, after a committed connector binding change and after a new or changed connector name is recorded, through a hook the gate library exposes (`Gate_connector_announce`) and the server installs at boot (#48090).
- The server announces `keeper_skill_activations_changed {name, trace_id}` after a skill activation ledger write appends: every write goes through a write lock whose commits call an observer once the session lock is released, and the server names the keeper from the registry (RFC-0483 L1, #48120).
- `GET /api/v1/keepers/skill-activations?keeper=<name>` answers with one keeper's skill activation projection alone, read from that keeper's ledger. The per-surface usage rows live on their own route, `GET /api/v1/keepers/skill-usage?keeper=<name>`, which returns `usage.state` of `ready`, `no_session`, `unavailable` (with `reason` and `detail`) or `no_catalog` (RFC-0483 L2, #48121).
- `POST /api/v1/tui/preferences` writes one parsed change to the `[tui]` table of runtime.toml (chat visit, theme, language, Board sort, candle, retired help hint) through the config commit, so it announces `runtime_config_changed`; a change outside the closed shape is refused with 400 (RFC-0482 L1, #48133).
- Ship the OpenCode Go subscription gateway in the seed runtime config: `opencode_go` provider, one DeepSeek V4.1 Flash binding with a probed reasoning contract, and the `go-deepseek-then-glm` worker lane. See `docs/operations/opencode-go-runbook.md`. (#48141)
- A model's capabilities block accepts `accepted-reasoning-efforts`, the probed list of efforts a categorical reasoning-effort wire takes from that model. The list reaches the resolved capabilities and answers the pre-dispatch refusal `has no declared categorical reasoning-effort contract` for a model the Agent Core catalog does not know (#48144).
- Add the OpenCode Go subscription gateway to the embedded model catalog: `opencode_go` provider plus six model rows with probed list pricing, context ceilings, streaming shapes, and advertised effort ladders, so keeper turns on Go bindings report cost. (#48145)
- `GET /api/v1/tui/preferences` answers the terminal's `[tui]` settings and `[voice.stt].send_on_stop` from the runtime.toml the server writes, as `masc.tui-preferences/v1`, without the rest of the file (RFC-0482 L2a, #48147).
- Dashboard Task creation keeps the request id in session storage and shows a confirmation panel that re-checks the server creation record before recreating, when the response was lost or the page was reloaded (originally #47915, fragment missing) (#48167).
- The TUI reads the `runtime_quota_spent` waiting source and marks a Keeper waiting on it with a `⊘ quota spent` roster badge, ahead of the server reporting a running Keeper whose every candidate has spent its quota (RFC-0484 L1a, #48168).
- The dashboard reads the `runtime_quota_spent` waiting source and draws it as 한도 소진 in the waiting panel, fleet queue, lane strip and lane queue (RFC-0484 L1b, #48172).
- The Keeper waiting inventory reports a running Keeper whose every candidate has spent its quota window as a `runtime_quota_spent` row due at the earliest stated reset, and its health section asks the operator to act with `runtime_quota_spent=<n>` while grading itself degraded (RFC-0484 L1c, #48182).
- `/health?full=1` has a `typesafeai` section graded from the latest outcome of each configured TypeSafe judgment server; a payment (402) or credential (401, 403) refusal is an operator action reason in the rollup (RFC-0484 L2, #48184).
- Every TUI footer leads with the server's operator action reasons as `ACTION NEEDED <n> · <first reason>`; the plain `/health` probe carries the last full-health snapshot's `overall_status`, `operator_action_required` and `operator_action_reasons` for it (RFC-0484 L3, #48186).
- The TUI Git changes title names the checked-out branch and its distance from the upstream (`main ↑2 ↓1`). `GET /api/v1/git/status` and `GET /api/v1/repositories/:id/changes` return a `branch` object read from `git status --porcelain=v2 --branch`, built by one shared function. A branch without an upstream, an upstream whose ref is gone, and a detached HEAD are shown as such instead of as zero counts (#48212).
- `GET /api/v1/tool-metrics/series` returns the retained tool calls grouped by hour or by day: calls, failures, total time, p50, p95 and max per bucket, plus the 20 tools that spent the most time. `since_hours` (default 24, at most 31 days), `bucket` (`hour` or `day`), `utc_offset_min` (so a day starts at the viewer's midnight) and `tool` select the window. A `tool` value that is empty or has leading or trailing whitespace is refused with 400. A bucket in which nothing ran is present with null latency. The read runs on the executor pool behind the 30 s live cache and on its own read-only SQLite connection, so tool-call inserts are not delayed (#48240).
- The Tools page has a "도구 실행 통계" card. From `GET /api/v1/tool-metrics/series` it charts calls and failures, total time, and p50/p95 latency per hour (24 hours, 7 days) or per day (30 days), shows the totals as tiles, and lists the tools that spent the most time. Pressing a tool name narrows every chart to that tool; the previous charts stay, dimmed, until the narrowed ones arrive, so the pressed button keeps the keyboard focus. A response for another window, bucket, offset or tool than the one asked is reported as an error instead of being charted. Buckets that the window cuts short at either end are left out of the charts and stay in the totals, and a bucket with no calls leaves a gap in the latency chart (#48248).
- `Authz_zone`, the writer zone that appends one record to the authorization log while masc runs. It opens the log and the external store itself, keeps their handles, and refuses a log that is not there or holds no `Fresh_bootstrap`; a log that is not there is refused before either file is opened. Each commit judges what an earlier entry left with the judgment that a start makes, and refuses to write when the store and the log disagree or the store holds no answer; a record that `Authz_state` refuses writes nothing. Otherwise it closes the earlier intent, writes `Intent_pending`, appends the record, publishes the state with the record and writes `Committed`. Before it aborts an intent it asks the file whether the log still ends where the intent began. No caller uses it yet (multi-account B3b, #48270).
- `Authz_log.confirm_end`, which says under the file lock whether the log still ends where this process left it and writes nothing. An end that moved stops the log, as a `Diverged` append does, and so does a log or lock that is not one regular file under one name. A lock held by another process, or a read that fails, writes no line and leaves the log open (multi-account B3b, #48270).

### Changed

- Extract private Board voting and vote-log effects from the aggregate module,
  preserving public APIs, write-ahead ordering and snapshot settlement policy. (#47378)
- Board persistence and Keeper/schedule fixtures explicitly initialize each fresh Board-writing root before its first store or live owner. Restarts, malformed-source checks, deletion retries, vote ledgers and replay assertions retain the same initialized source without preparing again. (#47458)
- The transferred schedule retry assertion includes the runner's existing due-for-retry disposition while still checking the exact resolved Keeper and shutdown operation. (#47458)
- Direct Board producer and healthy reader fixtures explicitly initialize their fresh source before the first store or live owner. Pure and negative subjects retain their setup, restarts reuse the initialized source, and the MSX fixture declares the existing shared preparation dependency. (#47466)
- The standalone Keeper Board ACK probe installs the actual native execution journal runtime under its root switch before driving native requests, matching server ownership and the existing checkpoint probe. (#47466)
- Goal verification can retry a matching pending request or reconcile its verdict while preserving submitted evidence; changed evidence is refused while verification is active (#47185, #47612).
- Refresh Keeper waiting inventory when schedule changes are published. (#47635)
- Revalidate pending confirmations on changes and expiry deadlines. (#47636)
- Keeper Turn Inspector follows asynchronous Skill results across original traces using the physical receiving turn, preserving original activation frames, ledger provenance and incomplete-scan gaps (#47649).
- The TUI no longer re-reads the open Keeper chat history on the 2s cadence; appended turns and revalidations owe the chat one read instead (#47654).
- CI의 Dune alias 검사에서 실행 명령을 로그에 남겨 빌드와 테스트 실행 단계를 확인할 수 있게 해요. (#47666)
- Keeper review guidance in `config/prompts/keeper.md` now carries the operator's 2026-11-02 review text, so the live `keeper` prompt override can be cleared and the file is the only source of the Keeper preamble again. (#47667)
- The TUI Fusion view no longer re-reads on the 2s cadence; it re-reads on `fusion_run_status` and retries a failed read with backoff (#47668).
- A lane fact the worker answered whole no longer blocks automatic browser selection: with the refusal alone automatic browse answers `no_available_browser`, and a healthy client of another transport on the same worker is still chosen with the refusal listed beside it. (#47695)
- The TUI observer decoder reads the names of the Keeper and installation question pushes, the async request push and the confirmations push from the server modules that send them (#47766).
- The server announces each record a Keeper's native task journal or child content journal appends, as `keeper_native_tasks_appended` and `keeper_child_content_appended` with the Keeper's name (#47790).
- The TUI chat pane reads its Keeper's native tasks and child content when the server announces an append for that Keeper, instead of on every 2s tick. A failed read is retried with growing waits (#47791).
- The Identity tab marks each service as attached (filled) or not (hollow),
  lists attached services first with a blank row before the rest, and
  takes `v` to show all, attached or unattached services and `o` to switch
  between attached-first and declared order. The cursor stays on its
  service when a reading, view or order moves its row. (#47795)
- `GET /api/v1/gate/keepers` and `masc_keeper_list` take `name=<keeper>` and answer only that Keeper's row (or its error row) with the name echoed, never from the list cache. On the route, a `name` that is missing its value, repeated or not a Keeper name answers 400 (#47798).
- `docs/rfc/RFC-librarian-lifecycle.md` section 4.10 says how Muse follows the
  boundary rule. A fresh session the provider refused leaves the refusal in
  that turn's record, and the next fresh session on the same runtime starts
  strictly past the refused start: at this turn's boundary, else at the newest
  atom. The implementation-state notes there and in the window RFC now match
  the code, including where the two lanes still differ. (#47801)
- A Keeper woken by a Board event or scope message is still told it cannot end the turn silently, but the wake clause no longer offers "leave the reason in one line if you do not handle it" as the way out (#47807).
- The Keeper Owner sends `keeper_row_changed` with the Keeper name after each metadata write it commits, after a write that raised, and after the write failure that fences its metadata store, so a roster reader can reread that one Keeper's row (#47810).
- The Keeper registry sends `keeper_row_changed` for a Keeper whose entry it added or removed, or whose phase or failure (reason or time) moved, from the one place a registry swap commits (#47812).
- Each execution receipt append sends `keeper_row_changed` for its Keeper to that workspace, since a roster row reads the newest receipt for its lane observation and blocker summary (#47814).
- Each runtime catalogue publication (startup, reload, setup-required, an assignment transaction, a rollback) sends `keeper_roster_changed`, since a roster row's runtime id and provider rest read the whole catalogue (#47818).
- `docs/rfc/RFC-deferred-contextual-memory.md` and
  `docs/rfc/RFC-0456-librarian-output-contract.md` say that each Librarian
  claim cites the observations it relied on (`evidence`), and the absorb gate
  asks each pair with only those observations. A pass no longer fails as a
  whole for size; a pair whose cited observations do not fit is asked the
  pair-only question and recorded as such. (#47847)
- 백로그 RFC 문서에서 도구 실행 뒤 요청에 다시 싣는 블록 목록을 지금 코드에 맞춰 네 종류(`Keeper_instructions`, `Active_goals`, `Completion_authority`, `Operator_note`)로 고쳤어요. (#47850)
- A Candle ledger append sends `keeper_row_changed` for each Keeper whose balance, equipment or account revision it moved, or `keeper_roster_changed` when it set the half-life (#47857).
- A provider rest record (rate limit, failed attempt, success, quota window) and a dated rest ending send `keeper_row_changed` for each Keeper whose shown rest moved (#47860).
- The TUI can read one Keeper's roster row (`GET /api/v1/gate/keepers?name=`) and put it in place in a complete roster; the reads that use it follow (#47865).
- When the deployment store check refuses stored state, the guide `docs/guides/DURABLE-STORE-HARD-CUT.md`, the preflight helper and `install-local-build.sh` give the fresh-state steps as: stop the server, delete what the change names, run the check again, install. Lane Add-on `fresh state` lines say delete, and a refused tool request owner names its whole scope: the owner record directory and the request body directory (#47866).
- The TUI reads a Keeper's roster row when the server sends `keeper_row_changed`, and the whole roster with `fresh=true` on `keeper_roster_changed`, a revalidation, a resumed authority, or two or more changed rows at once; failed reads retry with growing waits (#47868).
- The TUI reads a starting Keeper's roster row again when its `next_action` stops being `probe`, at its creation time plus `agent_staleness_threshold_s`, which `Keeper_status_runtime` now exports (#47870).
- Librarian claims answer `evidence`: the conversation positions shown as
  `turn=N`, the tool observation indexes the prompt now prints, and whether
  the counterpart block or the historical task contexts were used. An answer
  citing an observation its input does not have is refused. Fresh state: this
  binary reads no Librarian request record stored before it (the
  `keeper-librarian` scopes in `lane-addons/tool-request-owners`); stop the
  server, delete those records, and install. (#47873)
- RFC-0481 says the roster answer carries the Candle decay basis and the TUI computes balance, burned and circulating from it; the two-second roster read is removed after the time-driven values are in place (#47875).
- Keeper prompts list each Active Goal's latest review, latest measurement
  and `[yours]` or link-unreadable marker under a new `### Goal Observations`
  section instead of on the Active Goals rows. The Active Goals block in the
  System prompt now changes only when a Goal is created, updated or changes
  phase, so a measurement or a Task claim no longer sends the whole history
  uncached on the next turn's first request for agent-core Keepers. Requests
  after a tool call on OpenAI-compatible providers no longer carry the
  latest review or measurement; the Goal list and criteria stay. (#47879)
- The TUI computes Candle balances, burned and circulating from the roster's `candle_decay` when it draws them, so the amounts fall with the half-life between reads; it no longer reads the rows' `candle_balance_milli` (#47884).
- The TUI no longer reads the Keeper roster every two seconds; it reads the rows the server names, the whole roster on a roster change, a revalidation or a resumed authority, and owes a failed whole read a retry with growing waits (#47888).
- `validate-stores` proves a Librarian payload forest once per scan instead of once for every tool request owner record. Only a proof that passed is kept, so a record that depends on a broken forest is still refused for the same reason (#47889).
- `deployment_preflight_helper.exe validate-stores` gains `--jobs N`, which reads up to N stores at once, each in its own process. The default stays 1, reading one store after another as before. The report prints in store order for every N (#47890).
- RFC-0481 says the server announces `keeper_turn_changed` after the writes behind the turns answer, the TUI owes a turns read on it and on schedule, confirmation and fusion events owes a waiting read, and the two-second turns read is removed after the preview signal (#47892).
- The TUI reads the Keeper turns when the server announces `keeper_turn_changed`, on a revalidation and a resumed authority, and reads a failed turns read again after a growing wait; schedule and confirmation events read every Keeper's waiting list and a fusion run status reads its Keeper's (#47897).
- The TUI reads the Keeper turns when the server announces `keeper_turn_preview_changed`, so the answering badge and the chat pane follow a running turn's preview (#47901).
- The TUI no longer reads the Keeper turns every two seconds; it reads them on the server's turn and preview announcements, a revalidation, a resumed authority and after a failed read, and reads a failed waiting list again after a growing wait (#47902).
- The Librarian absorb gate asks each pair with only the observations its
  claim cites. A claim that cites nothing, or whose citations do not fit the
  request boundary, is asked the pair-only question, and every verdict records
  how it was asked. A pass no longer fails as a whole for size. Fresh state:
  this binary reads no Librarian request record stored before it (the
  `keeper-librarian` scopes in `lane-addons/tool-request-owners`); stop the
  server, delete those records, and install. (#47904)
- The TUI Verification queue no longer reads every two seconds; it reads on the request store, run registry and backlog announcements, a revalidation, and after a failed read (#47909).
- The TUI Repositories surface no longer reads every two seconds; it reads when the server announces the `repositories` dataset, on a revalidation, on arrival and after a failed read (#47918).
- A Keeper may hold several Tasks at once: a claim is no longer refused
  while the agent holds another Claimed or InProgress Task, and `claim_next`
  claims the next unclaimed Task instead of handing back the held one.
  Auto-claim and the claimable list include Tasks the Keeper created itself.
  Cancel no longer requires a reason (Keeper, `masc_transition` and the
  operator HTTP route), and release no longer requires a summary or, for a
  strict contract, a handoff. A `masc_transition` done on a Done Task is a
  no-op success (#47927).
- The TUI Schedules surface no longer reads every two seconds; it reads on `schedules_changed`, on `keeper_event_queue_changed` for a Keeper a drawn row reads, on revalidation, arrival and after a failed read (#47935).
- `internal_agent_runs_changed` names the run registry that changed (`verification`, `goal_verification` or `exact_lane`); the TUI Verification surface re-reads only for the verification registry (#47937).
- A new Goal may carry a `due_date` that has already passed; only a value
  that is not a `YYYY-MM-DD` calendar day is refused. (#47945)
- Dropping a Goal no longer cancels its unclaimed linked Tasks or sends a
  drop notice to the holders of claimed ones. Linked Tasks stay as they are,
  and the `masc_goal_transition` drop response has no `tasks` field. (#47945)
- Schedule and pending-confirmation changes are announced only as `schedule_store_invalidated` and `operator_pending_confirm_invalidated`; the duplicate `schedules_changed` and `pending_confirms_changed` announcers are removed, and the remaining path drops the fleet schedule list and operator snapshot caches before it publishes (#47959).
- The TUI reads schedule and pending-confirmation changes from `schedule_store_invalidated` and `operator_pending_confirm_invalidated`; its `schedules_changed` and `pending_confirms_changed` events are removed. A schedule change reads the agenda once instead of twice, and neither change blanks the waiting column while a read that began before it is still not taken as current (#47966).
- Turn records keep the provenance of each input token count
  (`input_provenance`), so a post-compaction context estimate is shown as an
  estimate in the TUI Context screen and the Dashboard instead of as a
  dispatched request (originally #47874, fragment missing) (#47968).
- The TUI agenda strip records an unread schedule change only on the owed schedule read; `schedules_agenda_event_pending` and its successor launch are removed. A newly opened observer or lost events read the agenda once instead of twice, any agenda read a change overtakes is still retired, and `r` reads the schedules once (#47969).
- The TUI agenda strip and the Schedules page each owe their own read, so a page read that answers first no longer settles the agenda's debt: an agenda read a change overtook is retired, a failed page read no longer leaves the agenda marked as possibly behind, `r` on a later page reads the page once, and `r` off Schedules reads only the agenda (#47975).
- The TUI no longer keeps a Gate receipt refresh flag: authority recovery already owes the Gate a read, so the extra read the flag started, which overtook the read already on its way and discarded its answer, is removed (#47978).
- The TUI Usage surface no longer reads transport health every two seconds; it reads it when the server's transport refresh loop pushes `transport_health_snapshot`, on arrival, on a revalidation and after a failed read (#47997).
- The TUI's Keeper logs view and Info tab read the shown Keeper's metrics when `keeper_metrics_appended` names it, after a failed read, and on a revalidation, instead of on every two-second tick (#48006).
- Goal store, verification ledger and measurement store writes now drop the planning cache and announce `goal_projection_changed` to the workspace's observers; ledger and measurement writes also advance the Goal projection generation (#48018).
- Merge 29 duplicate keeper type definitions into canonical `*_types` module
  aliases (batch #1, layer 1 of 5). Facade `.mli` structural restatements
  become plain aliases; groups with unqualified references are linked with
  compiler-checked manifests. No behavior change. (#48020)
- Merge 20 duplicate runtime/voice/gateway type definitions into canonical
  module aliases (batch #1, layer 2 of 5). No behavior change. (#48021)
- Merge 28 duplicate auth/server/workspace/tool/lane type definitions into
  canonical module aliases (batch #1, layer 3 of 5). No behavior change. (#48022)
- Merge 17 duplicate registry/metrics/profile type definitions into canonical
  module aliases (batch #1, layer 4 of 5). No behavior change. (#48023)
- Merge 4 duplicate TUI type definitions into canonical projection/grammar
  aliases (batch #1, layer 5 of 5). No behavior change. (#48024)
- A change in the verifier's in-process observations that the planning row shows (`verifier_unreconciled`) now drops the planning projection and announces `goal_projection_changed`; a scan that finds the same failures announces nothing (#48029).
- The TUI's Planning screen reads its Goals and Goals tree when `goal_projection_changed` or `execution_snapshot` arrives, after a failed read, on entering and on a revalidation, instead of on every two-second cadence pass (#48034).
- Every Ego answer, failures and refusals included, carries `inputReadiness`; the browser failure lead sentence now says whether the command was refused before any effect, failed after part of it, or has an unknown effect (#48042).
- A failed `BrowserAct` call goes back to the Keeper's model instead of ending
  the turn, as `BrowserInteract` and `BrowserGoto` failures already do
  (#48048).
- A running Codex Keeper turn is no longer asked to wrap up when a chat
  message is queued; it runs to its end and the Owner then starts the queued
  chat. Operator interrupt and chat stop are unchanged (#48051).
- The TUI observer reads the five payload-less workspace store pushes (schedules, pending confirmations, verification requests, Goal projection, repository catalog) as one `Workspace_store_changed` event naming the store; wire names and behaviour are unchanged (#48063).
- The TUI reads the Dashboard briefing only while Home is on screen; other surfaces no longer request it on every refresh, and the connection status and unreachable check count it only when it was asked (#48066).
- Keeper turns no longer measure every playground checkout before the
  prompt, and World State no longer carries the Repository Checkouts layer.
  The sandbox status surface still inspects checkouts on request (#48074).
- TUI copies (`y`, a drag selection, `/copy` and the other copy keys) go to `pbcopy`, `wl-copy` or `xclip` first when the TUI runs on the operator's own machine, and the notice names the tool that took the text. Inside tmux the text is also sent to the terminal as OSC 52, for an operator who attached from another machine. Over SSH, or when no tool is installed, every tool fails or the text cannot be written out for a tool, the text is sent to the terminal as OSC 52 as before, and the notice says why (#48077).
- The iMessage and Telegram connectors announce `gate_connector_changed` only when their poll state changes in what the connector list draws; a new iMessage cursor or Telegram offset alone announces nothing (#48092).
- Muse Code 1.4.14 sessions no longer log an MSP schema fingerprint warning when they open. The codec's conformance corpus now names muse-code-sdk `42c7658`, whose stable schema 1.4.14 reports; its transcripts are the ones the codec was already tested against (#48093).
- The Slack and Discord connectors announce `gate_connector_changed` when their connection moves to another phase or their startup error changes; a new Discord sequence number or reconnect backoff alone announces nothing (#48096).
- The TUI Connectors list and a Keeper's channels tab read the connectors when the server announces `gate_connector_changed`, and retry a failed read with growing waits; the refresh tick no longer reads them (#48114).
- The TUI reads its `[tui]` settings from the server at start (`GET /api/v1/tui/preferences`, bound to its own workspace) and sends every pick — chat visit, theme, language, Board sort, candle, retired help hint — through one ordered writer to `POST /api/v1/tui/preferences`; it no longer reads or writes runtime.toml itself. A failed start-up read opens on the defaults and says why once (RFC-0482 L2b–L2d, #48150).
- `masc config set` saves through the workspace's running server when one answers on the port for this workspace: it edits the runtime.toml text the server reads and saves it with the revision it read, so the server commits, publishes and announces it. A server still starting or a missing sign-in stops the command; with no server for this workspace it writes the file as before (RFC-0482 L3a, #48152).
- `masc web-search-setup` saves through the workspace's running server like `masc config set`, and shows the state of the text the server holds; with no server for the workspace it writes the file as before (RFC-0482 L3b, #48153).
- `masc voice-local-setup` sends its changes to the workspace's running server through the voice setup route, with the revision it read; with no server for the workspace it writes the file as before (RFC-0482 L3c, #48154).
- `masc tui` opened before its server is up reads the screen settings again when it first reaches the server, and leaves any setting picked in the meantime as picked (RFC-0482, #48160).
- `masc runtime-default-set` saves through the workspace's running server, making the edit its local write commits to the text the server holds; with no server for the workspace it writes the file as before (RFC-0482 L3d-1, #48164).
- `masc browser-lane-setup` plans and saves its bidi, automation and ego tables against the runtime.toml the workspace's running server holds, through that server; with no server for the workspace it writes the file as before (RFC-0482 L3d-2, #48173).
- `masc runtime-setup-batch` and `masc runtime-setup-inventory` read the runtime.toml the workspace's running server holds, and the batch publishes its validated text through that server; with no server for the workspace they read and write the file as before (RFC-0482 L3d-3, #48174).
- The TUI Config panes read runtime.toml when the server announces `runtime_config_changed`, on arrival (including `p` between Config panes and Lanes `e`), on a revalidation and after a failed read, instead of every two seconds (RFC-0482 L4, #48175).
- `GET /api/v1/keepers/skill-activations?keeper=<name>` now carries only the keeper's activation projection. The per-surface usage rows moved to their own route, `GET /api/v1/keepers/skill-usage?keeper=<name>`, which returns `usage.state` of `ready`, `no_session`, `unavailable` (with `reason` and `detail`) or `no_catalog`. Where L2 answered `no_ledger` on `skill-activations` for both a missing session and an unavailable ledger, this splits that into `no_session` and `unavailable`, so a reader of every keeper does not receive every ledger (RFC-0483 L3a, #48176).
- The TUI Activations pane reads the selected keeper's `GET /api/v1/keepers/skill-activations?keeper=<name>` as its own read, instead of the `skill_activations` field of `/api/v1/dashboard/tools` (RFC-0483 L3b, #48181).
- The dashboard Tools page reads the selected keeper's skill activations from `GET /api/v1/keepers/skill-activations?keeper=<name>` beside the tools answer, and shows them only when both answers name that keeper (RFC-0483 L3c, #48185).
- The dashboard Skills page reads every keeper's `GET /api/v1/keepers/skill-usage?keeper=<name>` after the catalog and joins the rows to the catalog by exact reference for its usage column and coverage line (RFC-0483 L3c, #48187).
- The TUI Usage pane reads every roster keeper's `GET /api/v1/keepers/skill-usage?keeper=<name>` while it is on screen and joins the rows to the catalog by exact reference (RFC-0483 L3d, #48192).
- The Skill proof harness reads the chosen keeper's `GET /api/v1/keepers/skill-activations?keeper=<name>` and stores the answer as `keeper-skill-activations.json` (ledger join: `keeper-skill-activations-{before,after}.json`). The evidence schemas are `masc.keeper-skill-use-proof.v3`, `masc.natural-keeper-skill-ledger-join/v3` and `masc.keeper-skill-tui-proof.v6` (RFC-0483 L3e, #48194).
- The server decides its account mode once at boot from the optional `account_mode` member of `config.json` (`"Single_user"` or `"Multi_account"`), the last mode event of `authz.jsonl`, and the external store that the install record names, returning every refusal reason; it boots only as a single user for now, and refuses a `Multi_account` request, a multi-account trace, an unknown `account_mode` value, and a base path whose external store says it was restored to before its bootstrap (multi-account A2, #48196).
- The TUI Usage pane keeps a keeper's last answer when that keeper's usage read fails and says the read failed. It draws rows for a revision outside the catalog reading on their own instead of dropping them, and says when the roster is empty, not read yet, or its read failed. A roster not read yet, or read with an error, no longer drops readings (#48199).
- The per-keeper usage and activations decoders in the TUI reject fields outside their schema (#48199).
- The Skill proof evidence names the activations projection instead of the Dashboard: proof `durability.activations_projection_equals_ledger` (`masc.keeper-skill-use-proof.v4`), join `ledger.projection_equals_durable` and `ledger.projection_kind` (`masc.natural-keeper-skill-ledger-join/v4`) (#48199).
- The composition execution journal announces `keeper_async_requests_changed` for its Keeper after each write it makes. The TUI reads an open async request detail again on that Keeper's announcement, and an open source Task body on the backlog's `execution_snapshot`, instead of every two seconds. Both also read again on a revalidation and after a failed read (RFC-0483 L4a, #48202).
- The TUI Tools view reads the Skills catalog, the selected keeper's activations and each keeper's usage on `keeper_skill_activations_changed` and `skill_catalog_published`, when their pane opens, and on a refresh or revalidation, instead of every two seconds. Switching keepers no longer reads every keeper's usage. The two-second tick reads only the selected keeper's tool inventory (RFC-0483 L4b-1, #48205).
- The authorization log is read into one state, `Authz_state`, that takes a `Fresh_bootstrap` mode event first and then `Off` and `Reactivate` in turn for the workspace of the bootstrap.
