### Fixed

- The installed server no longer rejects its own release receipt as `invalid_receipt` because of the `masc-exec-ssh-bootstrap` companion that the installer always installs, so `/health` reports the installed release as verified again. (#46474)
- Fixed obsolete completion rejection delivery after Task resubmission: fence queue publication by current authority, preserve delivered receipts for intake, and prevent stale unroutable releases from changing newer work. (#45493, #38059)
- Exact Add-on workers hold one request body during the first inventory after a start, and check that their store directory is unchanged when they answer from memory. A pending record that is missing, invalid or finished when read again, or a missing or invalid record in the first inventory, now stops the worker: every later call, observations included, fails with that reason without reading the store again. Transient I/O errors fail only that call. Non-regular records are refused without leaking a file descriptor, and errors safely quote record names. Package revisions move to workspace-curator 0.1.3, candle-appraiser 0.1.4 and keeper-librarian 0.2.2 (#45500).
- Show prompt authoring errors and original Markdown provenance in the TUI without changing body override behavior. (#45509)
- Document the offline fresh-state recovery required by delivery-specific
  official-client frontiers, including candidate helper identity, targeted
  session backups and validation before installation or rollback. (#45512)
- Keep denied Addon exports out of deferred loading while checking that separately admitted composition recovery controls remain usable. #45513
- Align TUI action fixtures with the context/incarnation contract and verify schemaless installation decisions without display-text snapshots. #45514
- Record actual selected Addon test failures, exact native artifact identity and preservation of the original 54 completion criteria. #45515
- Share candidate quota/rate standing across Keeper, CLI, Vision and HTTP Exact calls; retain admitted runtime identity across callbacks and preserve provider quota reset hints without creating ownerless failure marks. (#45522, #38061)
- Keep admitted verifier Read, Grep, media and layout operations on the endpoint whose path authority was captured, and correct the retained-worker fixture's model-facing file argument and evidence-store/workspace module references. #45524
- Record successful selected Addon reruns, verified native artifact identity and actual native On/Off/reconnect with original result/receipt preservation against original A01/A02 criteria, preserving remaining work and historical failures. #45528
- Refuse boot for Keeper metadata I/O failures observed during examination, even when quarantine is accepted; retain separate JSON and schema rejections for explicit quarantine (#45529).
- Recheck an ego snapshot target tab after selector waiting, refuse partial-text quoting after native whitespace, and document native ref refresh requirements. (#45535)
- Require an explicit observed live client for ego hand-off/take-over at the raw browser Add-on export, before browser selection. (#45536)
- Exact workers replace finished request input bodies with the original ID, digest and result, retaining the destination in multi-tool packages. Workspace Curator 0.1.4, Candle Appraiser 0.1.5, Keeper Librarian 0.2.3 and HITL Auto Judge 0.1.1 use worker record version 2; worker request/result JSON is unchanged (#45540).

- Preserve explicit live client identity for hand-off and take-over at both

- Restore each Task verifier's retained original, dispatch facts, exact judgment/domain notes and host commit receipt. - Enumerate both retained refusal stages in verifier attempt recovery so strict compilation checks the closed state coverage while preserving the existing retry and child-intent behavior. #45573

Retained old insufficient approvals, three bounded controls and a later revision-refuted replay do not establish eleven-case proof or production completion (#46021).

- Keep Settings reachable on short desktop screens by scrolling the navigation rail without shrinking its menu buttons (#46042, #46043).
- Bind companion origin/publication creation to mandatory private recovery and target capabilities, and reconcile unchanged pre-existing files without hiding cleanup or recovery-release failures. (#46049)

- Exclusive file creation now requires its paired recovery target and owner capability, stages and syncs the payload privately, then publishes with a descriptor-relative no-replace rename. Append-to-missing follows this boundary; existing-file append remains independent. Removed direct public-leaf creation and its partial-public-target state. (#46049)
- Standalone report exports use a stable owner in the destination parent's publication recovery registry. No-replace refusals discharge their exact obligation after cleanup; interrupted cleanup preserves typed cancellation evidence. (#46049)

- Cache decoded successor-recall transitions instead of raw journal JSON in `recall_journal_cache` and avoid re-decoding cached rewrite lines on every recall query (#46057, #46058).

- Dashboard API parser reads the top-level `code` field of server refusal bodies (`{"error": "...", "code": "..."}`) before falling back to the error sentence, so refusal-code branches like `workspace_precondition_failed` match again instead of showing the shared-editing hint. (#46059)

- Dashboard: the desktop keeper nav keeps its active marker visible — `overflow-y: auto` on the rail now comes with the marker drawn inside the item, so the `left: -10px` rail edge no longer clips it (#46065)
- TUI: in Korean input mode, letter shortcuts (j/k, q, i, d, s, ...) were silently dead — the terminal delivers the input method's Hangul character and no command spelling matched it. A command context now reads the two-set layout back into the Latin keys (`과` replays `r h k`), while every text field, the chat composer and the lane Add-ons drafts keep the Hangul as typed. Known limit: shift does not survive the input method, so uppercase shortcuts stay dead in Korean mode (#46066).

- Let Keeper provider/model changes retain canonical checkpoint history while deferring replay admission until the next caller query; only target-unselected foreign reasoning is excluded, and active mandatory replay remains protected. #46082

### Performance

- Index current tool-call identities once per TUI trail projection, preserving late results and superseded attempts without repeated full-list searches (#45549).
- Read incremental JSONL file identity, boundary and appended bytes through one descriptor, reusing unchanged boundaries (#45550).
- Return fresh Keeper observations directly from prepared execution snapshot reads instead of repeating their filesystem work in the HTTP fallback (#45595).
- Share tool-quality cache entries for identical positive-window queries regardless of the unused recent-count parameter. (#45633)
- Reduce repeated field-list searches when validating Keeper metadata keys with an immutable schema traversal, preserving duplicate priority, diagnostic order and current-schema completeness (#45645).
- Capture optional Keeper metadata with one descriptor and blocking read job, while preserving caller-context decoding and recovery reporting (#45652).
- Index blocked execution scopes within each Keeper queue observation while preserving full semantic validation, retry eligibility and queue order. (#45662)
- Transfer each completed, privately owned Lane retained-read buffer to its immutable result without a full-record copy. Keep the independent verification read, syncs and identity checks. Selected-reader interpreter checks preserve byte/error results and show roughly half the allocation in durable double reads; whole-server improvement remains unmeasured. (#45672)
- Build a projection-local Home action index so larger approval and question queues do not repeatedly scan and copy the growing decision list. Preserve action identity and first-seen order. (#45720)
- Replay Fleet broadcast recipient acknowledgements through a decoder-local index and restore the admitted recipient order once, reducing repeated list reconstruction while retaining the durable journal and recovery protocol. (#45721)
- Prepare the Home decision reading once per synchronous TUI Build so focus, scrolling and rendering share the same immutable projection. (#45735)
- Seek retained tool-metric timestamp ranges directly in SQLite, preserving inclusive bounds and row ordering while avoiding full-index scans for filtered windows. (#45737)
- Compact Keeper queue snapshot JSON after one construction and sanitization, retaining the existing formatter for accepted values that the compact writer rejects. (#45741)
- Index runtime-event handler starts during late-arrival attribution so larger diagnostic windows avoid repeated full event scans while preserving the existing attribution heuristic (#45764).
- Submit new provider-input blob publication through the existing shared I/O policy while preserving strict durability and ordered snapshot admission (#45777).
- Reuse strictly verified provider-input blobs across Keeper histories, preserving mandatory payload and parent sync when physical content must be republished (#45803).
- Reuse the Keeper checkpoint lineage for next-request forecasts while preserving exact carried positions, history bytes, and Librarian continuity. (#45837)
- Cache exact tool-schema wire byte counts in the existing weak JSON cache and reuse them in Keeper wake telemetry; add opt-in SDK timing and allocation measurement (#45914).
- Stream owned schema-observation reports through atomic output while preserving the decoded v1 value and event order. Report output now surfaces strict payload and parent-directory sync failures. (#45997)
- Reuse cached compact SDK schema byte counts when measuring the Keeper request reserve, preserving tool occurrences, escaped system prompt bytes and the existing worker boundary. (#46012)
- Prepare Keeper request reserve and fixed-prefix digest in one CPU worker job with a cooperative yield between the unchanged calculations. (#46034)
- The live machine frame route parses each published frame once and prepares its compressed body once per observation, so every watcher of the same frame is served the same bytes instead of re-serializing and gzipping 1.2 MB per poll; a matching `If-None-Match` answers 304 (#46195).
- `masc_dos_screen` accepts `include_frame=false` to skip the frame's RGB copy and PNG encode; the play seat poll, the invite list and the pad route use it, so watching guests no longer make the DOS worker PNG-encode a frame every 5 s each (#46196).
- The play seat no longer builds the handoff roster on every poll. `GET /api/v1/play/seat` reads only the caller's participation and the observed holder, and the roster that reads every credential moves to `GET /api/v1/play/participants`, which the play page reads when it opens and when a player opens the handoff selector (#46236).
- Reuse one strictly verified Librarian gate inventory during completed-history validation instead of rereading the whole gate scope for every original; recovery, publication and dispatch keep their fresh reads (#46242).

## [0.64.0] - 2026-10-23

### Upgrade notes

- 명시 Memory 후보는 이제 keeper-librarian Add-on 으로만 처리합니다. Add-on 이 붙어 있지 않으면 후보는 큐에 남고, Keeper 로그에 `Librarian explicit admission is off: no keeper-librarian Add-on is attached; N candidates wait` 가 대기 건수가 바뀔 때마다 한 줄 남습니다 (#45093).

### Fresh state required

- The automation cleanup descriptor now records the instance's profile
  directory, and a descriptor written by an earlier build is not read. The
  deploy preflight refuses each native claim slot under
  `.masc/lane-addons/native-claims/` whose current instance history carries
  such a descriptor (decoder `Browser_addon_socket.check_retained`), and lists
  the paths to set aside with it: the slot, and the binding and observations
  of the instance it names. Stop the server. For each refusal, end any process
  that still holds a file under `profiles/` of the `mb-…` allocation the
  history names in `cleanup_context.directory` (`lsof +D <allocation>/profiles`);
  an earlier build could leave a relaunched Gecko browser there (#45187). Then
  move aside every path the preflight lists and that allocation, and start the
  new build (#45403).

### Added

가이드 확인 기록: 작성자가 2026-10-23 PO의 컷 head `2a9f660f086e9cb8e9b0b423694d0fc83c5ad94c` 검색 보고를 확인했습니다. 보고의 범위는 전체 git tree 경로와 Markdown 경로 키워드(open_window, cookie, storage, ump, alphatex, vst, role, portrait, prompt, fleet, accessory), main의 관련 Markdown code search, 후보 문서 본문입니다. ‘가이드 없음’은 이 범위에서 사용 가이드를 찾지 못했다는 뜻입니다. 설계 설명만 있는 항목은 사용 가이드로 세지 않습니다. 검색 원문: MASC Board `p-ac45c699902228e98776559f2ac96584`, PO 댓글 `c-2b014ac505346d7d78b7e97ca391f082`(2026-10-23 10:40 UTC).

- Librarian Addon의 명시 후보 실행을 위해 원래 Keeper·Memory·후보·prompt·schema를 보존하고, host의 판단과 Gate 평가를 같은 원본으로 복원하는 포트를 추가합니다 (#45094).
- `masc_browser_act` takes `open_window`: it opens a new browser window and returns its tab's `tabId`. It works on the owned Gecko browser and on a connected BiDi Firefox (a background window the connection owns); the extension and Stagehand refuse it. ([#45271](https://github.com/jeong-sik/masc/pull/45271)) 가이드 없음 — 검색 범위는 위 가이드 확인 기록 참조.
- `set_viewport` on `masc_browser_interact` works on the owned Firefox: the window is resized to the asked viewport plus the browser's own chrome, measured again and corrected, and a size below Firefox's smallest window is refused with the size the page kept. Giving neither `width` nor `height` restores the window's first size. ([#45276](https://github.com/jeong-sik/masc/pull/45276)) Usage: [사용 가이드](docs/design/browser-lane.md).
- `masc_browser_read mode=cookies` on the owned Firefox also lists the page origin's `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` key names and its IndexedDB database names under `storage`, with counts (at most 100 names per area, each cut at 200 characters). No value is read. ([#45278](https://github.com/jeong-sik/masc/pull/45278)) 가이드 없음 — 검색 범위는 위 가이드 확인 기록 참조. 참고: [설계 설명](docs/design/browser-capability-parity.md).
- `masc_browser_act` takes `set_cookie` and `delete_cookie` on the owned Firefox. A cookie is set for the tab's own page host (the domain is not an argument), lives at most 7 days (a session cookie without a lifetime), and holds at most 4096 bytes; the value is never returned. Live BiDi, the extension and Stagehand refuse it. ([#45279](https://github.com/jeong-sik/masc/pull/45279)) 가이드 없음 — 검색 범위는 위 가이드 확인 기록 참조. 참고: [설계 설명](docs/design/browser-capability-parity.md).
- `masc_browser_act` takes `set_emulation` and `clear_emulation` on the owned Firefox: a tab's reported location (latitude and longitude, with its geolocation permission), language tag and IANA time zone. They go over the session's BiDi connection. Firefox 158 cannot reset a locale or time zone with null, so clearing sets back the values the tab had before. Clearing restores overrides only and preserves existing permissions; a location grant remains for the owned session. Live BiDi, the extension and Stagehand refuse it. ([#45283](https://github.com/jeong-sik/masc/pull/45283)) Usage: [사용 가이드](docs/design/browser-lane.md).

Residual buffered output is refused explicitly. (#45312) Usage: [사용 가이드](tools/vst/README.md).

- `BrowserAct` `block_requests` makes every request from a tab and its frames to the listed hosts fail as a network error on an automation Firefox, through a WebDriver BiDi intercept on that tab. `unblock_requests` lifts that tab's blocks, and closing the session lifts them all. Live BiDi, ego and Stagehand refuse both actions before any effect (#45413) Usage: [사용 가이드](docs/design/browser-lane.md)..
- `BrowserAct` `back`, `forward` and `reload` work on an ego connection, on the pages an agent opened in its task space. Reload is ego's `page.reload()`; back and forward read the tab's history through `page.cdp`, are refused before any effect when there is no entry that way, and answer once the tab is on that entry and its document has loaded. The text is cut at `maxChars` without splitting a surrogate pair, with `truncated` and the full length in `chars`. Other connections refuse it before any effect (#45461). - An ego connection reads and answers the JavaScript dialogs of the pages an agent opened in its task space. A listed row of a managed page carries the dialog blocking it, as a live BiDi row does; `BrowserAct` `accept_dialog` (with `text` for a prompt) and `dismiss_dialog` answer it with the dialog in the receipt, and are refused before any effect when none is open. A click or key input that opens a dialog answers with it, and a DOM input the dialog stopped is a partial effect with it. While one is open, reads, moves and input on that page are refused before any effect; closing the tab is not (#45486). Guide: `skills/browser-lanes/references/advanced.md`.

### Changed

- Librarian의 명시 후보를 Addon 원본 요청으로 실행하고 host의 absorption·Memory receipt·ACK로 연결합니다. 원래 실행 증거와 첫 Gate 저장 복구를 검사하며 purge는 남은 모델 실행도 취소하고 기다립니다 (#45093).
- 공유 Addon worker에서 요청 하나의 오류가 다른 Keeper의 처리를 막지 않게 하고, 대기 중인 원본과 새 후보 사이의 반복 self-wake를 방지합니다 (#45093).
- Retain complete original Librarian input data without provider/checkpoint projections, including nested parsed tool results, ordered speaker metadata and full working contexts. Explicit-candidate admission keeps its separate purpose checks (#45247).
- Preserve unfinished Librarian work as Pending without advancing Memory cursors or acknowledgements. Suspend later phases of the same wake and expose the distinct waiting state in Dashboard and TUI decoders (#45298).
- Resolve completed-history input, policy, prompts and schema once for both the original synchronous pass and immutable Addon preparation. (#45322).
- Retain same-read counterpart source rows, external deduplication evidence and read-only cursor observations without granting ACK authority. (#45323).
- Capture complete checkpoint and official-client source selections for the actual durable consumer; bind original messages to checkpoint bytes and preserve rich payloads separately. (#45324).
- Preserve the complete original history source while rebasing only current Memory, and retain independent full successor intent/acknowledgement facts. (#45324).
- Retain and resume original completed-history Addon requests with separate workspace, Memory and runtime identities; require actual host execution proof before publication. (#45325).
- Bind fresh-basis requests to their exact predecessor and require the parent’s complete confirmed successor before dispatch. (#45325).
- Share the original absorption evaluation journal between admission and completed-history adapters while preserving independent purposes and host proof checks. (#45326).
- Reject replacement-publication events as unsupported original Gate history. (#45326).
- Discover retained original request scopes through strict owned storage even when Keeper metadata is absent. (#45327).
- Expose derive_memory for completed-history proposals beside admit_memory; reject cross-purpose calls and preserve both original requests through worker restart. (#45328).
- Authorize completed-history provider work against its full original host request and wake that same Keeper after actual result delivery or Addon reattachment. (#45335).
- Recheck the complete acknowledged successor at initial host authorization and actual provider dispatch. (#45335).
- Revalidate retained source prefixes and compare the complete original Memory basis under the actual disposition write lock before creating new effects. (#45336).
- Expose typed locked basis supersession separately from uncertain disposition storage failures. (#45336).
- Publish original history through captured absorption judgments, source locks and actual Memory receipts; recover ACK and both source positions before durable Finished. (#45337).
- Close only known prepublication Memory-basis conflicts while letting actual original receipts take precedence. (#45337).
- Route production completed-history work through the configured Addon, resume originals before reselection, and suspend later phases on pending or blocked original publication. (#45338).
- Resume a single durably linked fresh-basis successor; refuse missing confirmed children and retain actual race and child-loss integration scenarios. (#45338).
- Keep terminal refusal reasons visible while permitting fresh selection of unread history, and report unavailable Addon attachments without acknowledging source or inventing Memory effects. (#45338).
- Publishing the exact-output registry can now count an Addon lane toward a required service: an Addon lane whose exact output carries the service's id (for example `hitl_auto_judge_exact`) and holds an admitted slot serves it only when the caller also names that id in the new `addon_served_lane_ids`, which defaults to none. A `runtime.toml` table with the right name is never enough on its own, because it loads without any installation behind it. The registry keeps the list whole and a replacement inherits it. Nothing passes the list yet, so every required service still needs its builtin slot until a later layer attests an Addon that dispatch routes to (#45356).
- 실제 Candle Python worker의 도구를 Keeper가 검색·로드·호출하는 deferred 경로와 Off·재연결 시 원래 요청 및 권한 보존을 검증하는 통합 검사를 추가합니다 (#45357).
- Librarian 스택을 최신 요청 저장 계약에 맞춥니다. Gate 재시도는 본문을 먼저 보존한 뒤 digest intent·원본 레코드·ACK 순서로 복구하고, 목록과 본문 복원 및 권한 불확실성 처리를 구분합니다 (#45357).
- The HITL Auto Judge request now has a named immutable original, `Hitl_judge_original`: the approval id, input hash and sequence with the system prompt, output contract and context bundle, encoded with a closed field set and a digest that ignores key order. It carries no authority or effect, and the approval's decision stays with the host. The worker builds its three judgment messages through the same module, so the original and the request it sends cannot drift. Nothing routes a request through the original yet, so behavior is unchanged (#45365).
- A HITL judge original can now be retained in the host's original-request store, `Lane_addon_tool_request_owner`, one record per approval attempt (`<approval_id>#<sequence>`) with the request body stored once by digest and a summary of the approval id, input hash and sequence. Restoring checks the request, the attempt identity, the summary and the destination, and a second input for the same attempt is a conflict. It records what was asked and nothing that authorises an effect; the decision, terminalisation and consumption stay with the approval queue. Nothing retains an original yet, so behavior is unchanged (#45369).
- Share semantic pointer resolution, resolved URL decoding and default drag waypoints across native browser adapters. #45398
- The Gecko automation backend runs each session on its own profile, which
  masc creates under `<lane-addons>/gecko-profiles/` and passes to Firefox with
  `-profile`, and removes under that profile's lock when the session ends.
  geckodriver no longer gets a fixed Marionette port, so each browser picks
  its own. A session whose browser reports another `moz:profile` is refused
  (#45403).
- Distinguish the TUI feature inventory from Plugins, preserve original navigation targets, and show explicit reselection notices. (#45415)
- Publish builtin UI roles once from the server inventory for Dashboard and TUI; retain package role ownership and exact action identities. (#45416)
- Exercise generated media Origin admission and bearer read authority through real HTTP route scenarios. (#45420)
- Group the TUI package browser by manifest role, with one presented order for rendering, selection, Enter/Right and refresh. #45457
- Remove the synthetic Dashboard Performance playground and static Cockpit/Inspector overview pages. Inspector opens server configuration directly, and retained focus mode keeps its exit control and full content width (#45466).
- An ego connection runs all its commands in one `ego-browser nodejs` process instead of one per command. The process connects back to a Unix socket in the connection's private directory and answers each script over it, so a page's dialog and event state in ego's SDK lasts from one command to the next; on ego lite 0.6.0.16 a dialog that outlived its process made every later command to that page time out. A command that does not answer in time, writes past the output limit or is cancelled still stops the process with its group, and the next one starts another (#45485). Guide: `docs/rfc/RFC-browser-live-ego.md`.
- Show the declared worker service and role in the TUI install preview, without inferring either from the other. #45488
- Clarify that metric writers prepare child directories beneath an already initialized workspace ownership root. (#45506)
- Restore release-record omissions for previously merged Add-on validation changes. (#45517)
- Document pure Add-on hook validation and the caller's observation responsibility. (#45518)

### Fixed

- Workspace Curator 와 Librarian 이 같은 submit-once 모듈로 원본 요청을 worker 에 넣습니다. host 가 보내기 전에 거절한 제출은 "결과 모름"으로 남지 않고 다음 pass 에 다시 제출됩니다 (#45094).
- VST sessions reject malformed, unknown and duplicate completions, preserve failed-host outcomes against late replies, and enforce the 16 MiB response limit in UTF-8 bytes across stream chunks (#45286).
- The isolated monitor-worker fixture includes the quantization and captured-time dependencies required by its copied runtime modules (#45286).
- Failed VST sessions include their retained stderr diagnostics when the host closes, while preserving the original error, cause and code (#45376).
- Preserve the original Connector event identity in durable Keeper chat, Dashboard provenance, and TUI history without inventing operation or turn ownership. (#45378)
- Acknowledge Slack ingress only after durable acceptance of its original route and input; recover the earliest recorded route on retry and preserve failures without acknowledgement. (#45379)
- Include timing and note-transform modules in isolated Worker lifecycle test fixtures. (#45381)
- `masc browser-lane-setup` commits its runtime.toml tables one after another. A table refused after another was written now prints the written tables and their next steps before the refusal, which names its own table, and the setup wizard no longer says nothing was written. A replan refuses an automation or ego table that someone else wrote since the plan instead of overwriting it (#45389).
- The browser capability scenario test expects the owned Firefox driver to claim `set_viewport`, which #45276 added. It failed on main because it still asserted the opposite (#45402).
- Declare browser emulation numeric bounds as TOML floats so tool schema initialization does not abort deployment preflight and application startup. #45405
- `masc` built from a main that carries #45283 starts again: the `masc_browser_act` tool definition writes the `latitude`, `longitude` and `accuracyMeters` bounds as floats, which the definition loader requires (#45406).
- Preserve typed Task submission denials and return actionable claim recovery without losing owner resubmission or verification supersede behavior. (#45407)
- Decide Task submission ownership under the backlog lock instead of a separate tool-layer snapshot check. (#45408)
- A Gecko browser that leaves its automation worker, for example by
  relaunching itself to apply a staged update, no longer blocks the browser
  Add-on. On each configuration pass the host looks at the Gecko profiles of
  instances whose record says the allocation was released, or that no record
  names. It removes a free profile under its lock, sends SIGTERM to the
  process that holds one, and SIGKILL if the same process still holds it 70 s
  later. A profile it keeps is an issue of the configuration reading. The
  allocation is released without a worker-written receipt (#45411).
- Restore Dashboard test typechecking by removing unsupported role-query options while preserving exact accessible-name matching. (#45412)
- Group Plugin Inspect by role and preserve exact worker/installation targets across Flow, technical, history and action-menu transitions. (#45417)
- Apply the shared admitted-Origin policy to generated media responses while preserving authenticated read authority. (#45419)
- Scan original Task history in bounded 64 KiB line slices while preserving physical offsets, continuation anchors, captured prefixes and ordered source failures. #45422
- Let Task history reads finish under their existing view/workspace cancellation scope instead of failing at the shared ten-second HTTP deadline. #45423
- Enumerate classified and unclassified Plugin category drift states explicitly so the TUI compiles with fragile-match warnings treated as errors. #45426
- Open a new phrase from an empty or unselected arrangement. Missing clip
  metadata no longer throws before the phrase editor opens; explicit and
  matching-source MIDI pattern selections retain their existing behavior (#45432).
- A Gecko automation worker that can no longer address its browser session
  now ends instead of refusing every command until it is detached: a session
  creation that raised, a command timeout included, failed in transport or
  answered without a session id, an `invalid session id` reply, or a driver
  that exits while the worker serves. A creation the driver refused is not a
  loss, and a loss during the worker's own stop does not interrupt it. The
  runtime replaces the worker, and the host's Gecko profile pass ends any
  browser it left (#45433).
- Multi-tool Exact workers retain the tool identity of bodyless admission refusals and reject reads or retries through another tool, including after restart. (#45437)
- Retain invalid prompt surface metadata and its declaring file as typed authoring diagnostics without interrupting prompt rendering or overrides. (#45438)
- Pass the retained request summary when dispatching a captured Add-on tool request, fixing a partial-application compile error (#45444).
- Transfer pooled HTTP client cleanup ownership only when the idle queue accepts the client or its daemon receives a close signal, including cancellation during release. (#45445)
- Preserve realtime voice session intent and history when its bridge endpoint is unavailable, and report retained suspended sessions as inactive in Keeper responses (#45448).
- Keep an uncertain Librarian host result on its original unread-source frontier, preventing a later wake from creating another provider request for the same pending work (#45451).
- Require owner readiness before a supervisor promotes a runtime or reports it healthy, and document store recovery boundaries. (#45455, #37900)
- Keep canonical snapshot hashes only on source-guard frontiers, removing unused whole-history encoding and hashing from Codex and Claude Code turns. (#45458)
- Restore Addon test compilation by declaring the filesystem dependency, covering replacement journal events and connecting actual MCP fixture exit observers (#45462).
- Exact Add-on workers (Workspace Curator, Candle Appraiser, Keeper Librarian) no longer read and hold every retained request body on each submit, listing and observation. A worker reads its store once at start, one record at a time, then reads only pending requests, so finished classification records no longer push the Curator worker toward its 128 MiB limit. Package revisions move to 0.1.2, 0.1.3 and 0.2.1 (#45469).
- Keep speculative Add-on schema validation pure so losing oneOf alternatives do not emit rejected logs, counters or span events. (#45474)
- Declare the Skill configuration library used by the actual deferred Addon worker test so the selected fixture can compile. #45477
- Enumerate native-session context delivery and acknowledgement cases explicitly so resume validation compiles with fragile-match warnings treated as errors, preserving its existing canonical snapshot checks. #45480
- Preserve completed Board mutations when Activity Graph projection fails; report the failed projection separately in result metadata. (#45489)
- Initialize the Board/Task regression fixture's workspace before recording its authoritative Task metric. (#45504)
- Honor operator-retained Browser Add-on allocations before decoding backend configuration, so older persisted payloads cannot block an explicit handoff or subsequent recovery. Preserve instance, child-settlement and allocation-identity checks. (#45511)

### Internal

- Add `masc.private_browser_profile`, which captures the process that holds a
  masc-private browser profile's lock and is the only module that may send it
  SIGKILL. A captured holder keeps no descriptor for the lock file, so releasing
  it never drops masc's own lock, and Chrome's private profile removal now lives
  there as well (#45391).
- `Workspace_memory_revision` stores a ledger or Briefing state once under the SHA-256 of its bytes in `workspace-memory/revisions/<kind>/`, and reads it back only when the bytes hash to the name, decode as that kind and re-encode to the same revision. Writes and reads stay under the workspace base and refuse a symbolic link below it. Nothing calls it yet. The ledger digest now has one definition, `Workspace_memory_ledger.sha256`, and the Briefing digest moved from the execution capture to the revision module; digest values do not change (#45454).

## [0.63.0] - 2026-10-23

### Upgrade notes

- `workspace-curator` is now package revision 0.1.1 and `candle-appraiser` 0.1.2, because both ship the shared Exact worker. Rebuild both worker images and install the new package revisions (#45200).
- Requests the workspace-curator worker still lists after its originals are moved aside end as `not_allowed` on the first host cycle, so the hard cut keeps that worker state (#45275).
- Metrics responses add outcome/observation counts and nullable rates; the handoff metric is `handoff_task_success_rate` and its fitness component is `handoff_task_success`. Consumers must use the current contract; raw metric storage remains unchanged (#45292).

### Fresh state required

- Workspace curator classification batch snapshots are now `workspace.memory.classification-batch.v3` and v2 snapshots are not read. With the server stopped, move aside `<base>/.masc/lane-addons/tool-request-owners/5e5665b70b1920c0c1dc7d16ab2b33c8d21773a7a0fab71bed62b03a8dd851e3/` (the workspace-curator original scope) (#45199).
- Workspace curator captures are now `workspace.memory.execution-capture.v3`, classification batch snapshots `workspace.memory.classification-batch.v4`, Briefing batch snapshots `workspace.memory.briefing-batch.v2` and observer registration receipts `workspace.memory.observer.registration.v2`, and earlier records are not read. With the server stopped, move `<base>/.masc/lane-addons/tool-request-owners/5e5665b70b1920c0c1dc7d16ab2b33c8d21773a7a0fab71bed62b03a8dd851e3/` (the workspace-curator original scope) out of `<base>/.masc/lane-addons/` (#45214).
- Original Add-on request records are now `lane.addon.tool-request-owner.v4`. A record names its request body by digest and keeps the consumer's summary of that request (#45246), and the body is a file under `<base>/.masc/lane-addons/tool-request-bodies/`. Earlier records are not read, and the deploy store check refuses each one by file. With the server stopped, move every scope directory under `<base>/.masc/lane-addons/tool-request-owners/` out of `<base>/.masc/lane-addons/` (workspace-curator is `5e5665b70b1920c0c1dc7d16ab2b33c8d21773a7a0fab71bed62b03a8dd851e3/`, candle-appraisals is `730f334f72479a09ad59258948bf7ed64bbe4d707bc3c0d1e787baeebe5d7a37/`). Candle retains each appraisal again under the same request ID and reads its retained answer from the `candle-appraiser/` worker state, so keep that state (#45228).
- Existing nonempty `<base-path>/.masc/metrics/` directories without the current `store.json` and per-agent `identity.json` bindings are refused. Back up and remove that metrics directory during a separately coordinated transition before recording into fresh state; no automatic conversion is provided (#45268).

### Added

- Keeper status reports the ext4 state of each image-backed Keeper volume under `sandbox_live.volume_filesystem`, from the server's last superblock read on the maintenance pulse. When a volume starts recording errors, the server posts one Internal System_post in the `sandbox` hearth with the error count and the first and last error (#45146).
- When a Keeper work volume records ext4 errors, the server repairs it the next time the Keeper is idle: it removes the Keeper's guests, clones the image to `<image>.pre-repair` with `clonefile`, runs `e2fsck` in a one-shot helper, and reads the superblock again to decide the outcome. An existing backup or an unknown helper image stops the repair before the guests are removed, and once the operator removes that backup the next idle pulse repairs the volume; a failed clone stops it before e2fsck. A damaged build volume is left for the next boot, which recreates it. Each repair writes a `masc.keeper.volume_repair.v1` receipt and a start and a result post in the `sandbox` hearth, and Keeper status shows a work volume's backup under `sandbox_live.volume_filesystem[].repair_backup` (#45168).
- The browser lane knows ego lite (`ego_lite`) as a live connection over an `ego_task_space`. It reads only: tab listing, text, elements, scene and screenshots, numbered by ego's page labels. Capability listings and automatic browser selection include it (#45234).
- The browser Add-on worker serves one ego lite task space as a live connection when `runtime.toml` names `[browser.live.ego]` `command` and `space`. Each command runs `ego-browser nodejs` once; detaching ends the space. Removing the table, or `[browser.live] enabled = false`, turns it off (#45235).
- An ego connection serves `open_tab`, `BrowserGoto` and `close_tab` on pages an agent opened in its task space. A tab the operator opened there is refused before any run (#45236).
- Quantize only selected piano-roll note attacks with `:quantize-notes GRID`, preserving lengths, dynamics, other notes and original MIDI clocks in one undoable edit. (#45253)
- Set or relatively shift selected note attack velocities with `:velocity-notes VALUE` and `:velocity-add-notes DELTA`, preserving release dynamics and rejecting invalid selections as one transaction. (#45254)
- An ego connection serves `BrowserInteract` on pages an agent opened in its task space: click, `click_at` with any button, double click, hover, `scroll`, `scroll_at`, fill, `select_option`, `follow_link`, `type_text` and `press_key`. Targets and guards run the same page scripts as the BiDi connection; ego sends the mouse and keys. Drag, touch, zoom, viewport, tab activation and frames are refused before any effect (#45256).
- A connected BiDi Firefox reads text, elements and the iframe list inside an iframe: `masc_browser_read` with `framePath` and `mode=frames` now works on a live BiDi connection, for a cross-origin frame too. New live capability `frame_read`; the extension does not serve it. ([#45263](https://github.com/jeong-sik/masc/pull/45263))
- Explain exact decimal and fractional timing for phrase, imported MIDI, arrangement and step-input experiments. (#45265)
- Compose globally voice-led chord progressions directly in imported MIDI tracks using their original PPQ/SMPTE units, with explicit routing, transactional overlap checks and one-step undo. (#45295)
- Document imported MIDI voice-led composition and verify saved experiments through harmony analysis, MIDI export and editable arrangement handoff. (#45296)
- `masc browser-lane-setup --mode ego` writes the `[browser.live.ego]` table of `runtime.toml`. It finds `ego-browser` on `PATH`, then in `~/.local/bin`, and writes it only when `--version` names ego lite's and Chromium's versions. `--ego-command` and `--ego-space` name another; a table that is there keeps its values. `masc prerequisite-actions ego-browser` reports ego lite, ready only when it names those versions, and on a Mac opens its download page (#45302).
- `masc setup`'s "5 · Give imp tools" checklist shows an unmarked ego lite row when `ego-browser` answers. It runs `masc browser-lane-setup --mode ego` and needs no Firefox (#45303).
- Set or adjust selected note lengths with `:duration-notes` and `:duration-add-notes`, preserving native MIDI releases and exact beat/frame units through Undo/Redo, MIDI export, harmony analysis and arrangement handoff. See [the piano-roll guide](../tools/alphatex/README.md#phrase-sequencer). (#45309)
- Add exact selected passage timing ratios with `:stretch-notes RATIO [ANCHOR]` for phrases and original PPQ/SMPTE MIDI. Preserve source events and reject invalid changes as one undoable edit. (#45339)
- Document exact passage stretching, its anchor and rejection rules, and source-TUI evidence through harmony analysis and editable arrangement handoff. (#45340)
- Record installed simultaneous audio/MIDI capture and native-parent passage stretch evidence, including clocks, hashes and explicit physical-device and intermediate-state limits. (#45344)
- Edit captured MIDI2 per-note controller, pitch bend and poly-pressure data at full 32-bit resolution, preserving original addresses and clocks through history, native playback preparation, arrangement save/reopen and raw export. (#45351)
- Explain native MIDI2 expression selection, exact raw32 edits and reset/history behavior, with bounded Worker, source-TUI and actual CoreMIDI receive/cleanup evidence. (#45352)
- Edit native UMP message times and explicitly selected MIDI2 note releases while preserving original event identities, authored clock provenance, portable variants and the shared playback span. (#45370)
- Document native UMP event time and explicit note length editing, with Worker, source TUI and private CoreMIDI evidence and remaining sequencer limits. (#45371)

### Changed

- An answered workspace curator classification root now leads to twice its fact count only when it held the count it was prepared for. A root the frame or a short backlog stopped keeps that count, and a root that filled the frame leads to filling it again, so a briefly short backlog no longer shrinks later batches. Each classification batch snapshot records the size it was prepared for (#45199).
- A workspace curator capture stores the model input once. A restore builds the input again from the stored batch and renders the prompt with the captured template; the capture keeps only the SHA-256 of the prompt it sent and refuses a restore that renders a different one. A Briefing batch snapshot keeps how many unconsumed entries it selected instead of a second copy of them. The observer registration receipt names the capture by its request digest instead of holding a copy, so an original's owner record holds one copy of the model input instead of six. The captured ledger still holds the claim and conflict texts a classification input cites (#45214).
- An original Add-on request body is written once, before the record that names it, and a record moves together with that body. Retain and progress compare the request by its digest. A Workspace Curator successor intent names its child by request ID and request digest instead of holding the whole child capture. A record whose body is missing, changed or not canonical JSON is an error, not absence (#45228).
- An original Add-on request record keeps the consumer's summary of its request, written once at retain like the request and refused when it is not in canonical form. The Workspace Curator summary (`workspace.memory.execution-summary.v1`) names the predecessor and the physical workspace that captured the original, and for classification the size the batch was prepared for and the selected facts, for Briefing the selected count and the SHA-256 of the prepared state. A restore computes the summary again from the capture and refuses a record whose summary differs (#45246).
- Document Curator CPU-isolation evidence and the limits of standalone scheduling measurements. #45260
- Share exact native-tick snapping and original/new overlap decisions for piano-roll note quantization. (#45280)
- The Keeper prompt now says when to register work: work that will not finish this turn becomes a Task the Keeper creates and claims, including requests given in conversation, and work that needs several Tasks or PRs is grouped under a Goal with a metric the judge can open and a target value. It names how to link Tasks (`goal_id` at creation, `masc_task_set_goal` afterwards), record progress with `masc_goal_measure`, and ask for verification with `request_complete` (#45287).
- A Workspace Curator pass moves each chain of originals that no pass reads again out of the scope, into `tool-request-owners-settled/<scope digest>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/` under the UTC date its root's ID was minted. A chain moves once its leaf is Finished or Conflicted and every original in it has both observer receipts acknowledged. The latest answered classification stays, since it sizes the next batch, and so do a Briefing that prepared the current Briefing state and every Rejected original. A request the worker still lists for a moved original ends as `not_allowed` (#45300).
- Loading an original Add-on request reads its record and the body it names under one hold of the scope lock, so an original moved between the two reads is found gone, not reported as a lost body (#45300).
- The deploy store check (`validate-stores`), which runs beside a live server, counts a Lane Add-on record that is gone by the end of its check as absent, as it already did for one gone before its read. A settle moves the record and then the body the check reads next (#45300).
- Define Keeper stopping authority through explicit cancellation, Gate, queue and terminal/failure state rather than repeated-call or text counts; mark the corresponding audit item as source-only pending runtime validation. (#45314)
- Explain signed MIDI input IDs, paired WAV/UMP take playback, output routes and state-restoration limits; link the existing arrangement and practice workflows. (#45343)
- Share Escape ownership and IME composition checks across Dashboard overlays and the command palette; import the keyboard policy directly from its source. (#45364)
- Remove redundant compact-viewport checks from TUI surface handlers already covered by the shared compact input dispatch. (#45366)

### Removed

- The `ego-browser` Lane Add-on and its host companion Skill. The live ego connection serves the same work to Keepers (#45257).

### Fixed

- The shared Exact worker now answers a submitted request that no listing reply could carry with the typed `input_refused`/`request_body_refused` result instead of an untyped tool error. The host narrows the batch instead of leaving the original pending with an unknown outcome. The refusal is kept without the request body, so a read after a lost reply gives the same answer, and the request is never listed (#45200).
- The shared Exact worker looks a submitted request up before checking the frame, so a request it already holds keeps its answer after the declared frame changes (#45200).
- The browser lane check tells a browser Add-on whose attach failed
  (`invalid`) from one the server is still starting or has not applied yet
  (`needs_verification`), reading how the configuration maintenance pass
  last applied its declaration. A switched-off browser declaration beside
  one that could not be read is no longer reported as off (#45222).
- The dashboard's browser client list reads its BiDi host paragraph with
  the same access as its clients, so one response never names an
  installation the list cannot see; the setup check reads the Add-on as
  the native host poll does (#45222).
- A Lane Add-on start that the engine refused, or that found its slot held by another container, no longer leaves a detached record once its release is confirmed. Execution authority is recorded before every create, and since #44214 it alone kept the record, so a start that kept failing added one binding per maintenance beat, which #38387 had removed. A record is now dropped when the release is confirmed and the worker never held a resource or committed an observation. An instance the operator retained (`Native_retained`) keeps its record. (#45229)
- Feed retained-request SHA-256 calculations in bounded slices so a large Digestif C call does not hold the server domain lock for the whole input. Original bytes and content addresses are preserved; installed latency remains to be measured (#45242).
- Reuse the current Curator pass's validated original inventory when there is no successor recovery to perform. Actual recovery still rereads and validates the complete forest, and execution and settlement still reload their original owner (#45243).
- Reuse validated immutable Add-on observer receipts when advancing their state instead of encoding, decoding and hashing them again; preserve exact acknowledgement and transition checks. (#45249)
- Decode retained Add-on progress events once before folding them, reducing repeated receipt hashing while preserving strict wire, payload, acknowledgement and state-transition validation. (#45250)
- Keep Curator classification preparation on the CPU pool instead of bypassing its isolation on a raw system thread. #45259
- Parse decimal and fractional musical positions in exact native ticks so valid decimal onsets and triplet input do not fail from floating-point rounding. (#45264)
- Distinguish missing agent metric observations from unreadable or malformed sources, retain exact query names, and expose absent fitness values as null (#45267).
- Store exact agent metric identities in SHA256-keyed slots with complete immutable binding publication and explicit recording outcomes (#45268).
- Keep Board posts, comments, and votes in Board activity instead of fabricating zero-duration successful Task performance records (#45269).
- A Lane retain whose `retained` record write fails no longer answers that nothing changed: an atomic replace can fail after its rename, so the operator now gets a runtime failure that says the allocation may already be retained and the next cleanup pass records what it finds, while a refusal still means nothing was written. A retain refused because a browser child reservation was never published now says the next cleanup pass fences it. The Chrome and live BiDi backends read their child claims through one shared module (#45216, #45272).
- A Lane Add-on worker that lists a request whose host original is gone no longer stops every host cycle at that request. The Workspace Curator authority answers such a request as unowned: it ends as `not_allowed`, the worker drops it from its listing, and the requests listed after it run. A request that does not match the original owning its ID, or whose owner cannot be read, still stops the cycle, and nothing is written under that ID (#45275).
- Include exact timing and quantization modules in the installed music bundle, and load copied music entry points before publishing the launcher. (#45280)
- Phrase and imported MIDI track quantization now use the same exact timing and new-overlap checks as selected notes, preserving original clocks, note lengths and release events. (#45281)
- Stop and replace a Lane Add-on worker whose process ended on its own, so its declaration starts a new instance instead of keeping the dead one as applied. (#45290)
- Count distinct observed Task IDs, separate completed and successful outcomes, and preserve missing metric denominators as null instead of fabricated zero/perfect rates (#45292).
- Use the latest terminal timestamp per Task and count contradictory latest outcomes or start times as `conflicting_tasks` without blocking other Tasks or agents; reject invalid durations or relationship identities; retain raw observation counts and name handoff-related Task success separately from transfer delivery (#45292).
- Keep unobserved Task outcomes distinct from measured zero values in agent details, validate the exact named fitness response including unresolved Task conflict counts, and label handoff-related Task success without claiming delivery receipts (#45293).
- The checklist's extension row no longer says that choosing it with the BiDi row is refused as ambiguous: a request that names no browser connection goes to the BiDi browser (#45303).
- Refuse MIDI quantization that newly crosses an unclosed note attack, including same-tick releases across tracks and attacks masked by existing overlap diagnostics. Preserve original overlaps and independent ports, channels and patterns. (#45308)
- Keep repeated browser input, equal tool receipts and repeated assistant text deliverable without synthesizing a Keeper turn stop; retain explicit scope, queue and terminal-effect boundaries. Remove obsolete repetition setup and buffers. (#45313)
- Keep secondary chat text readable after color projection and theme changes; retain typed tool status glyphs and Results colors without parsing rendered tool prose. (#45316)
- Dashboard 아티팩트 직접 진입에서도 작업 공간 authority를 읽고 후속 execution publication을 구독합니다. (#45329)
- 스킬과 런타임 설정의 authority 의존 화면 8곳에서 직접 진입 시 초기 조회와 execution 구독을 연결합니다. (#45330)
- Index original-MIDI attack ranges during note quantization and selected length edits, preserving actual event-order overlap decisions while avoiding a full comparison of every same-key note pair. (#45332)
- Assemble original-MIDI note and metadata patches once per edit batch, retaining source bytes, patch/insertion order and existing validation while reducing long-selection edit latency. Include a reproducible manual measurement runner. (#45333)
- An `ego-browser` refused for naming no versions is quoted to at most 400 bytes of what it printed, in the readiness JSON, the setup error and the worker's start failure (#45346).
- Normalize enhanced-terminal Enter, Tab, Backspace and ASCII control punctuation to the key vocabulary consumed by TUI forms, chat and navigation. Package browsing accepts legacy Backspace bytes as well. (#45347)
- Leave unsupported or malformed enhanced-key modifiers unclaimed instead of turning them into plain or Ctrl actions. (#45347)
- Keep Ctrl-T available for the chat queue and use F2 for terminal mouse ownership, including overlays. (#45348)
- Preserve surface inspection with i before entering an unfocused composer. Hidden forms and Add-ons no longer accept keyboard writes behind the terminal resize fallback; retained drafts and paste ownership remain intact. (#45348)
- Keep IME confirmation keys from executing Dashboard commands, messages, Board posts and inline configuration changes. (#45349)
- Match IDE search only within its actual focus owner and scope Copilot Escape to its dock, preserving unrelated modal and browser shortcuts. (#45349)
- Leave composing or previously consumed Escape with its owner across Dashboard dialogs and popovers. (#45354)
- Match declared shortcut modifiers exactly and use the same admission for the lazy command palette as the mounted host. (#45354)
- Keep runtime TOML save and indentation from consuming IME confirmation keys or previously handled events. (#45354)

### Performance

- A progress event on an original Add-on request reads and rewrites only its record, not the request. The record still holds the consumer's summary (#45246) and the commit's before and after domain states. Before, each event read, compared and rewrote the whole request (#45228).
- Original Add-on request discovery reads records only, not request bodies. A Workspace Curator pass takes each original's domain, held-back facts, Briefing state and the next batch size from record summaries, and restores a capture only for the original it advances, a size-refused leaf that could be halved and an original whose observer receipts still need work. An observed finished original costs one record read per pass (#45246).
- A Workspace Curator pass reads its active work, its refusals and its last answers instead of every original the workspace has retained (#45300).
- Reuse the SHA-256 already computed for an evidence blob's durable leaf when returning its immutable reference, avoiding a second hash of the same original bytes (#45305).
- Reuse one digest throughout a sampling blob's canonical publication and recovery fallback, preserving its complete original bytes, ownership checks and durable-publication requirements (#45306).

### Documentation

- Record reproducible native color-module measurements across 53 TUI themes and four color depths, including startup NO_COLOR policy and explicit screen-verification limits. (#45317)

### Internal

- `Keeper_volume_filesystem` reads a Keeper volume's ext4 error state from the host image's superblock: the kernel's Errors detected bit, the error count, and the first and last error's time, function, line, inode, block and cause. The image path comes from `container volume inspect` (#45143).
- The browser Add-on owner holds one live connection per transport, so a BiDi Firefox and an ego task space can attach to one worker (#45235).
- Remove dead `Tuple`/`Variant` Yojson pattern matches in `browser_observation.ml`, `keeper_msg_async_record.ml`, `keeper_projection_change.ml`, and `keeper_tool_plan.ml`. yojson 3.0.0 cannot construct these variants, so the branches were unreachable; explicit `Yojson.Safe.t` annotations replace them (#45273).

## [0.62.0] - 2026-10-22

### Upgrade notes

- A Keeper Firefox that is already running keeps the environment it was started with, tokens included. Quit it once after the deploy; the next server start opens one with the new environment (#44532)
- `MASC_DASHBOARD_CTX_HANDOFF_IMMINENT`, `MASC_DASHBOARD_CTX_PREPARING` and `MASC_DASHBOARD_CTX_HIGH` have no effect any more; unset them (#44618)
- The TUI rejects a `last_outcome` without `selected_runtime_id`, so a TUI built from this change cannot read the Lanes screen or the Keeper Info execution rows from a server that predates it. Restart the server on the same build as the TUI (#44666)
- Incomplete or malformed original-request records are refused explicitly. This storage foundation does not enable the production Curator Addon or replace its required host provenance, recovery journal and semantic validation (#44924).
- `scripts/install-local-build.sh --with-browser-addon` is removed. The script installs `masc-native-addon-launcher`, `masc-browser-addon-worker` and `masc-browser-process-owner` with masc by default and then declares the browser Add-on for the workspace; `--no-browser-addon` leaves all of it out. A workspace that already declares the package with another copy keeps that declaration, and setup names the `manifest_path` line that switches it. A workspace with no config root yet is installed, and the script prints the setup command to run after the first server start (#45099).
- The first `install-local-build` with this check stops while Lane Add-on records remain that this build's runtime refuses (on 2026-10-22 the live workspace held 10 action receipts with a string executor and 5 Exact requests with string messages). Stop the server, move each path a `fresh state:` line lists aside, run the install again, then start the server (#45170).
- `scripts/install-alphatex.sh` now installs the VST host inside the viewer
  runtime; `scripts/install-vst-host.sh` and the `masc-vst-host` launcher are
  removed. Rerun `scripts/install-alphatex.sh` (Python 3.12+ for VST). An
  existing `~/.local/bin/masc-vst-host` is no longer used (#45190).

### Fresh state required

- Retained Lane Add-on execution records and action receipts now use the `execution_authority`/`resource` record shape and object executors: before installing this revision, empty Lane Add-on state and remove leftover containers manually; records written before #44214 do not read. (#44214)
- A direct operation that is waiting for a Gate approval, or recovering one, when this release is installed makes the whole operation store of its Keeper unreadable: its stored record still names a `session_scope`, the store refuses that record with an integrity error, and the Keeper claims no queued operation and settles no running one until the record is gone. Resolve every pending Gate approval of a direct operation and let it settle before installing. If this release was installed first, install the previous build again, resolve the approval, then install this release. No such record existed in the live stores when this was checked (1,301 semantic rows, none naming a `session_scope`). (#44436)
- AgentCore checkpoint format is now exactly v13 with required usage coverage. Existing Keeper canonical files `<base-path>/.masc/traces/<trace_id>/<trace_id>.json` written with an older version are treated as superseded: the host starts without their saved history and its next successful save rewrites that file with fresh v13 state. No manual deletion is required. There is no converter or migration; this can discontinue an existing continuation. No live checkpoint reset, replacement, installation or server restart is performed by this change. #44780
- Workspace curator classification snapshots use `workspace.memory.classification-batch.v2` since #45135, and an earlier snapshot does not read. Every retained Curator original is restored on each pass, so one earlier record makes Curator discovery fail every pass. Before installing a build with #45135, turn the `workspace-curator` installation off, stop the server, and move every file under `<base-path>/.masc/lane-addons/tool-request-owners/<sha256 of "workspace-curator">/` to an archive. Finished originals count too (#45140).

### Added

- Validate installation-selected Addon input and output contracts around worker tool calls. (#44153)
- Add live host-process Addon worker ownership with shared MCP contracts, cancellation cleanup and foreground process-group release receipts. This component does not yet enable native package selection or move the browser executor out of the server. (#44175)
- Bind retained tool results to their canonical execution, enclosing Direct or Autonomous turn, and unique raw invocation before full result redaction. File paging and TUI consumption remain separate follow-up work. (#44181)
- Read retained original tool results in the TUI call reader with exact execution binding, verified byte paging, printed Execute output, and preserved reading state when refreshing fails. (#44190)
- Added a native Addon admission library and launcher with durable installation/resource claims, single-use execution identities, kernel-bound graceful termination, and confirmed process-group settlement. Runtime installation selection remains a separate follow-up. (#44192)
- Native Addon workers now require durable slot admission and the host launcher, verify the exact kernel owner before publishing tools, and stop owned processes independently of blocked ownership checks. Release requires confirmed retirement and settlement; Runtime installation selection remains a follow-up. (#44198)
- Retry durable retirement for the same exited worker without replaying its command after a transient cleanup write failure. (#44198)
- Run native Addon installations with durable ownership, typed resource receipts and restart cleanup. (#44214)
- Read complete music status messages and recovery paths with Ctrl-L, retaining command drafts, instrument selection and ongoing work. (#44220)
- Copy the whole readable Code file with `y`, preserving original source bytes separately from display rows and reporting OSC 52 delivery without claiming terminal acknowledgement. (#44232)
- Add revision-bound workspace file save API for Code editing, with Admin/workspace checks, pinned directory publication and durable recovery; draft/editor UI is still pending. (#44269)
- Edit Code source through the configured editor, compare and retain session drafts, and save against the captured server revision with explicit conflict reconciliation. (#44284)
- Choose a captured VST instrument/preset for arrangement MIDI assets with `i`, then audition trimmed, repeated and overlapping region/port instances alongside WAV backing through the audio output. Saved sound and undo retain original MIDI bytes. (#44323)
- Select or disable a package's named LLM Exact Outputs per installation with `exact_outputs`, independently of tool input/output validation. Selections retain package schemas, canonical order and effective worker revisions; undeclared or duplicate names are refused. (#44347)
- Show projection, verified instance-render counts, and mixing while preparing VST arrangement playback; retire progress on stop, project changes, and completion. (#44349)
- Run Gecko automation in the optional browser Add-on, with host-selected private profiles, typed readiness/session inventory, orderly detach and retained cleanup evidence after interruptions. (#44364)
- Keep every image and completed Mermaid diagram in the loaded chat available through `/images` and `/images N`, preserving the selected source and requiring a fresh list after changing Keeper or workspace. (#44374)
- Connect selected Exact Output declarations to the shared private host-request broker for native Add-ons, reusing typed Add-on lanes, retained attempts and the common server runner. Selection off disables the host port; retained answers can reach a replacement without another model call. (#44376)
- Export a complete arrangement to float WAV with `:wave FILE`, combining verified audio and selected VST sounds with exact frame placement, cancellation cleanup, and no replacement of existing files. (#44387)
- Export arrangements with `:export FILE.mid`, retaining reconstructed MIDI expression, independent region ports, original source provenance, measured timing precision, and cancellable file publication. (#44396)
- Connect owned Gecko read-only element selection to the browser Add-on's selected `locate` Exact Output. Recheck original and fresh observations before returning node references, keep model explanations separate, and preserve command cancellation and detach. (#44400)
- Preview declared image parts from MCP resources in the TUI with original inline payloads and resource-scoped selection. (#44409)
- Let Add-on packages grant request-specific model schemas while retaining the package output baseline, request identity and unknown-outcome evidence. Bind schema authority to browser worker configuration and validate new and duplicate model receipts against the original request's partial shape. (#44418)
- Search music library names and paths while preserving the selected source across refreshes, cancelled searches and editor returns. (#44422)
- Add the Stagehand session model callback through the browser Add-on's shared Exact Output broker, preserving schema authority, conversation roles, reported usage, cancellation and retirement. Chrome backend installation remains separate. (#44424)
- Give the browser Add-on owner independent Gecko and Chrome registrations and retain each original cleanup result. Retirement fences both routes, joins both cleanups and preserves uncertain in-flight input without replay. Actual owned Chrome startup remains separate. (#44431)
- Add a dedicated browser process owner that preserves its native lease independently of child descriptor handling and ends its own foreground group on keepalive loss, termination or child exit. Chrome session/profile integration remains separate. (#44438)
- Read published Markdown reports and HTML source in TUI Resources, alongside MCP resources, using the existing admin API and verified fixed revisions. (#44439)
- Navigate published report revisions in TUI Resources while preserving the chosen version across catalog refreshes and rejecting superseded reads of the same revision. (#44445)
- Connect Chrome/CDP/Stagehand sessions to the native browser Add-on, with fresh child admissions and private profiles, selected shared Exact Output, and confirmed owned-process cleanup. (#44451)
- Search loaded Resources documents with `/` and `n`/`N`, using the same document projection as display and preserving match position across last-page scroll clamping (#44456).
- Select and copy exact original text parts from Resources detail with `(`/`)` and `y`, preserving multipart content and reading ownership (#44477).
- Keep a configured dedicated Chrome profile across browser Add-on retirement and replacement. Native shared-profile admission prevents concurrent MASC launches, while original-child cleanup preserves profile data and cannot target a successor. - A voice capture opens the input device the operator picked (#44906).
  - Usage:
    - What: the recorder (`rec`) runs with `AUDIODEV` set to the saved `[tui] audio_input_device`; the voice panel names the device it used, and a recorder that runs and fails shows sox's own stderr with the device name.
    - Enable: set `[tui] audio_input_device = "<device>"` in runtime.toml (a name `AUDIODEV`/sox accepts). No key keeps today's default input.
    - Off: remove the key or set it to `""`.
    - Failure symptom: with a wrong device name the capture fails and the failure bubble carries sox's error text plus the picked device; with sox absent the capture fails as before.
    - Example: `audio_input_device = "USB Microphone"` in runtime.toml, then start a voice capture from the voice panel.

- Add regression source coverage for receiptless health observations followed by admitted report reads, receipt refusal, and foreign or booting workspace refusal. The scenarios have not been executed. (#45065)
- Preserve exact-run registry startup replay and payload-sweep observations, with separate successful unlink, directory removal and failed root-entry counts. (#45079)
- Add an Admin workspace-bound diagnostic GET for immutable exact-run startup replay and payload-sweep observations, without changing the run-list schema or performing cleanup on reads. (#45080)
- masc carries the browser Lane Add-on package. `Browser_addon_setup` writes it to `.masc/packages/browser` and declares it in `browser.toml` when the workspace has no declaration of it; an existing declaration is kept and two are refused (#45097).
- `masc browser-lane-setup --mode addon` writes the browser Add-on package this masc carries and declares it. Every other mode does the same after its host step, reports a refusal of that step and goes on; `--no-addon` skips it (#45098).
  - Usage: `masc browser-lane-setup --mode addon --base-path <absolute workspace path>`
- Refuse, before the previous server is stopped, a workspace that has a browser lane host installed and no enabled browser Add-on declaration: `masc-deployment-preflight-helper validate-browser-addon`, run by the deployment preflight that `scripts/install-local-build.sh` and `scripts/deploy.sh` already run. The local install passes `--browser-addon-declared-by-caller` when it installs the Add-on, since it writes the declaration right after the swap; with `--no-browser-addon` the check applies. Such a server answers every native browser host poll with HTTP 503. ([#45105](https://github.com/jeong-sik/masc/pull/45105))
- `click_at` takes a `button` (`primary`, `middle` or `secondary`), so a live BiDi connection and owned Firefox can right-click and middle-click; Stagehand and the WebExtension refuse a non-primary button before sending input (#45111).
- Stagehand `click_at` sends the middle and secondary button as the pinned 4.1.0 runtime's `page.click` `options.button`, instead of refusing it before input (#45112).
- `set_viewport` sets a tab's page viewport size (width and height, 100 to 4096 CSS pixels) on a live BiDi connection or Stagehand; on live BiDi, giving no size restores the browser's own size (#45114).
- A connected Firefox serves `back`, `forward` and `reload` on a named tab, and `close_tab` for a tab the same connection opened with `open_tab`; an operator-opened tab is refused before any browser call (#45115).
- `tap_at` and `swipe` send a touch pointer (not a mouse) from the same observed points `click_at` and `drag` use, on a live BiDi connection or the owned Firefox; Stagehand and a connected WebExtension refuse them before any effect (#45116).
- A connected Firefox's `tabs.list` rows carry `windowId`, so tabs that share a window can be told apart and the windows listed (#45118).
- `BrowserRead mode=console` reads an owned Firefox tab's console messages and uncaught errors from the BiDi `log.entryAdded` event, oldest first, keeping at most 200 per tab and reporting how many older ones were dropped (#45120).
- `BrowserRead mode=network` reads an owned Firefox tab's requests from the BiDi `network.*` events: method, address, state, and status, mimeType and bytes once completed, at most 200 per tab with the rest counted. Header values, cookies and bodies are never returned, only header names, and every query value in the address is replaced with REDACTED (#45122).
- `BrowserRead mode=cookies` reads the cookies an owned Firefox tab's page can see, at most 200: name, domain, path, secure, httpOnly, sameSite and expiry. The value is removed before the answer leaves the driver module (#45123).
- `masc_browser_interact` action `select_option` chooses the option with a given `value` in one single-choice `<select>` (`selector`), on a connected WebExtension, a live BiDi connection, the owned Firefox and Stagehand. A multiple select, a missing, repeated or disabled option and an element that is not a select are refused before any effect; the select gets `input` and `change` events, not a trusted click. ([#45150](https://github.com/jeong-sik/masc/pull/45150))
- `masc_browser_interact` `fill` types into a `contenteditable` editor (for example the Slack reply box) by selecting its content and inserting the text; it was refused as not a text input. New refusals: `editable_rejected_text`, `editable_changed_text`. ([#45188](https://github.com/jeong-sik/masc/pull/45188))
- The phrase grid draws the playhead, follows it while playing, and gives the
  cursor and playhead positions as bar and beat. Imported MIDI bar lines follow
  its time-signature map (#45194).
- In the phrase editor, `{` and `}` set the loop to the bars under the cursor,
  `<`, `>` and `:bars N` change a phrase length by bars, and the ruler numbers
  the bars and draws the loop range (#45195).
- A connected BiDi Firefox shows the JavaScript dialog a tab is blocked on as `dialog` in its `list_tabs` row, and `accept_dialog` / `dismiss_dialog` answer it on a tab the connection opened. New live capability `dialog_answer`. ([#45196](https://github.com/jeong-sik/masc/pull/45196))
- `masc_browser_interact` takes `framePath` (observed outer-to-inner iframe selectors) for `click`, `fill`, `select_option` and `scroll` with a selector on the owned Gecko browser. It replaces the iframe input that `masc_browser_act` had on that browser. Checked on Firefox 158 in a same-origin and a cross-origin iframe. A live connection, the extension and Stagehand refuse a framed request before any effect. ([#45198](https://github.com/jeong-sik/masc/pull/45198))
- `framePath` on `masc_browser_interact` also works on a connected BiDi Firefox: the frame's own browsing context receives the page script and native pointer input, for a cross-origin frame too. ([#45202](https://github.com/jeong-sik/masc/pull/45202))
- `masc_browser_read` mode `elements` takes `within`, a CSS selector: only controls that match it or sit inside a match are returned, with `within` and `withinMatches` (how many elements matched) in the answer. It works on the owned Firefox, live BiDi, Stagehand and the WebExtension (0.9.0). An invalid selector is refused as `invalid_css_selector`. An extension older than 0.9.0 ignores `within`; BrowserRead and the add-on's `browser_command` refuse that unscoped answer and do not pass its controls on. ([#45204](https://github.com/jeong-sik/masc/pull/45204))
- A live WebDriver BiDi connection serves `masc_browser_goto` with `lane = "live"`, its `clientId` and the `tabId` of a tab it opened with `open_tab`. A tab the operator opened, a missing `tabId` and a URL that is not HTTP(S) are refused before any effect. A WebExtension connection does not navigate and is refused as a selection. ([#45206](https://github.com/jeong-sik/masc/pull/45206))
- A live WebDriver BiDi connection serves `masc_browser_interact` action `activate_tab` through `browsingContext.activate`, after checking `expectedUrl`. Firefox also gives the browser window system focus, which the WebExtension's activation does not. A tab that is not the observed page in front afterwards is reported as a partial effect with what was read. ([#45207](https://github.com/jeong-sik/masc/pull/45207))
- The operator can retain a native Lane Add-on instance whose cleanup could not be confirmed, with `POST /api/v1/lane-addons/retain` (operator credential only). The host first confirms the admission and each Chrome and live BiDi child claim settled and the allocation kept its recorded identity, then records the acquisition as `retained` and the instance as detached with `Native_retained`, so the declaration starts a new instance. Nothing is inferred and no leftover file is removed. This replaces stopping the server and moving the instance's records by hand when, for example, a Gecko build relaunches itself outside the worker's process group (#45187, #45216).

### Changed

- Show Work and Keeper metadata read phases and correlate their actual I/O, optional Task comparison, caller and UI state application with the original source request. (#44143)
- Keep local-read detail logs under the existing routine level, skip suppressed JSON formatting, and record changed facts instead of repeating complete snapshots. (#44143)
- Export the shared pending-read phase text used by the Work and Keeper screens. (#44143)

- Show original Keeper metadata read and retry status in the composer and startup Overview, and explain creation-refresh coverage with the same typed decision that controls message availability. (#44155)
- Share Addon MCP admission and tool contracts independently of the worker execution engine. (#44167)

- Prepare only key-required recipient and draft data instead of the full display composer on every key. (#44177)

- Show the previous voice capture awaiting completion after withdrawal. (#44186)
- Distinguish a pending conversation save from an unknown save outcome on Home. (#44199)
- Abnormal process termination can lose queued, uncommitted conversation-visit persistence; the FIFO and its receipts are session memory. (#44199)
