### Performance

- A chat or turn events page reads the rows it serves, not the whole journal:
  paging through a 36.1 MB journal the way the TUI loads a turn puts 151 MB
  on the major heap instead of 6,086 MB and takes about 0.7 s instead of
  1.05 s (#43417).
- Remove a duplicate health request from full and scoped TUI refreshes. The enclosing request verifies workspace identity after all readers settle; collected readings remain separate from the verified result accepted by the UI. (#43447)
- Let a warm TUI refresh apply workspace-attested operator confirmations before unrelated readers finish. Share the original listing receipt with final delivery, retain workspace/action checks, and record the early state-admission clock without another HTTP request. (#43451)
- Share repeated node field definitions in composition prepare and run recipes while retaining each call shape. Correct negated required-group and anyOf exclusions in shared Tool input validation so mixed selectors are rejected by the presence check. (#43452)
- Admit the first ready matching TUI workspace before unrelated surface readers finish. Issue fresh question, approval and Keeper roster requests under the admitted workspace, and open the saved Keeper chat on its owned roster response. Retain the final workspace check and add an initial-admission observation clock. (#43454)
- Bind inline Overwrite/Append Write leaves to their original physical file resources so independent existing targets and new files under different existing parents can overlap. Preserve real parent creation conflicts, hard-link ordering, original Gate/publication paths and Task/parent receipts. Paths that need parent creation retain ordinary execution. (#43455)
- Let navigation load its required TUI data while an unrelated full refresh is still running. Keep dataset-specific ownership so late full results and cleanup cannot replace or release newer navigation reads. (#43457)
- Show the current surface's pending dataset and record source outcomes with request and UI application clocks for Before/After comparisons. (#43457)
- Start a destination's TUI navigation reads while earlier navigation collectors are still pending. Track each collector independently so late or duplicate completion cannot release another request or restore older identity authority. (#43458)
- Bind independent log-filter reads to the same dataset owner as full/navigation reads, preventing older pages from replacing the selected filter's result. (#43458)
- Record navigation collector start, UI settlement, refused authority and remaining collector count separately from data application. (#43458)
- Inline recipe Overwrite/Append nodes can now retain the deepest existing physical
  ancestor when parent directories are missing, so writes under disjoint existing
  ancestors can overlap while shared ancestors remain ordered. Preparation creates
  nothing; the original Write boundary recomputes missing directories before Gate,
  retains predecessor bytes for Append, and refuses redirects outside its claimed
  ancestor. The original Task/leaf receipts, publication recovery and async replay
  requirements remain authoritative. Feature scenarios are authored but unexecuted;
  parser checks do not establish runtime performance. (#43461)
- Share one complete presence inventory per frozen backend route among unchanged
  held jobs in a maintenance pulse. Each job retains its original authority; a
  fresh private read scope avoids borrowing another job's CLI. Large inventories
  use complete pipe captures, and positive visibility still requires full
  per-job inspection. Source comparison and authored scenarios are documented;
  runtime speedup remains unmeasured. (#43467)
- Resolve shared Task Skill references once under the captured Tool descriptors
  and reuse the immutable selection for identical snapshot/descriptor objects.
  Changed or mixed inputs reproject with existing stale/unreadable behavior.
  The Skill flow guide records the source comparison; runtime timing remains
  unmeasured. (#43476)
- Share one immutable Skill catalog, diagnostics and inventory preparation across
  Task prompt surfaces, executable setup, effective Tool projection and original
  Composition continuation setup. Retained turns survive interleaved preparations;
  inventory folds exact prepared entries without per-item whole-list searches.
  Changed source or Tool objects still reproject. The guides record the source
  Before/After comparison; runtime timing remains unmeasured. (#43480)
- A checkpoint save returns what reading its own bytes gives, and a read can
  fill the encoding memo with each message whose encoding is the document's
  own JSON. The first save after a read then encodes only the new messages
  and the ones this build writes differently (#43572).
- A Keeper turn starts from the decode of the checkpoint the Keeper last wrote
  or read while the file keeps its (device, inode, size, mtime), instead of
  reading and decoding the whole canonical file. With four 113 MB checkpoints
  and six turns each, later turns load in 0 ms instead of about 1 s and save
  in 224-356 ms instead of about 1 s; the store holds about 2.3 times the
  file size per Keeper (#43573).
- The Librarian continuity prefix hash runs on the shared CPU pool, so the next-request forecast no longer re-encodes a Keeper's covered history on the main domain (1.2-1.8 s for a 107.7 MB prefix) while every other request waits (#43593).
- Validate Keeper composition tool names without constructing schema-only Tools, and share the common descriptor/Skill name projection across both model surfaces. Per-Skill byte profiles construct only the declared composition schema; executable schemas and request bytes retain their contracts. Source operation counts decrease; runtime latency remains unmeasured (#43633)
- Share one immutable Keeper declaration projection among eligible Composition continuation intakes in a maintenance pulse. Later pulses and explicit resumes read anew; per-run ownership checks and typed declaration failures remain separate. Declaration reads use the common I/O executor policy. Runtime speedup remains unmeasured (#43648)
- Share pending Runtime catalogue reads across catalogue consumers and accumulate explicit refresh/post-save demand into a fresh follow-up, reducing overlapping catalogue requests without adding key-handler waits. (#43706)
- Prepare Runtime catalogue rows, configured route and checked Keeper assignments from one validated snapshot instead of decoding the snapshot twice; run pure catalogue interpretation through the existing shared response-decode CPU path while preserving validation and independent usage errors. (#43707)
- Share one response-owned provider-usage interpretation between Overview Runtime catalogue and quota observations while preserving independent early/late catalogue failures, usage errors and quota identity provenance. (#43708)
- Poll only unresolved original configuration owners while retaining complete immutable histories, uncertainty and recovery gates; skip irrelevant form-footer and absent-focus history searches without changing visibility or input decisions. (#43788)
- Transfer fully resolved named Inline Write and Read/Write resource claims through the existing outer SDK preparation path, preserving original source, Gate, physical conflict ordering, cancellation cleanup and async replay restrictions. (#43791)
- Retain producer-owned ready file scheduling inside mixed ordinary Compositions, separating opaque settlement barriers from file/data success dependencies and preparing current physical bindings after those barriers. Preserve original Tool contracts, Gate, receipts and async replay restrictions. (#43794)
- Reuse one execution-local Composition dependency-layer value for batch construction and ready binding order, avoiding repeated graph reconstruction while preserving original resource, failure, Gate and cancellation boundaries. (#43795)

- Extend the OCaml refactoring backlog with durable stream-media lifecycle evidence, five retained media boundaries and an explicit Board rearm ticket-ownership design, keeping source scope separate from execution proof (#43471).

- The glossary now defines "Isolated Job": the Docker-backed work started by `keeper_job_start` with a private workspace, no network, Keeper or host identity, credentials or workspace mounts, only checksum-verified input artifacts, and a durable `job_id` read back by `keeper_job_status`, `keeper_job_cancel` and `keeper_job_result` (#43519).
- Distinguish executed history/store suites from adjacent unexecuted checks in the OCaml refactoring inventory, and record the exact media validation request and its later focused result (#43528).
- Refine the evidence refactoring candidate around the complete reviewer input, distinguish stored snapshot checks from transport projections, and specify the missing authority-loop reproduction before implementation (#43538).
- Synchronize markdown documentation with v0.51.0-v0.58.0 runtime contracts and remove stale command, env, and configuration claims. (#43599)
- The glossary now has an entry for the `가이드 없음(...)` guideless marker that release notes leave at the end of Added bullets: it names the target document when one is known (`가이드 없음(대상 문서: <path>)`) or says `가이드 없음(문서 없음)` when no document is planned, and `scripts/release/count-guideless-added.py` counts the marker into `guide-metrics-<tag>.md` so the gate decision has the number (#43850).

### Internal

- Separate Memory OS snapshot codecs and consistency validation from persistence, preserving the public API and stored bytes (#43347).
- Give Memory OS journal encoding, decoding and dashboard row projection a private interface while preserving receipt recovery and append ordering (#43348).
- Model Memory OS successor recall with immutable revision maps and typed lineage, preserving replay, retirement and provenance semantics; document the responsibility boundaries and remaining refactoring candidates (#43353).
- Reduce provider usage reports into immutable per-account observations while preserving source-specific snapshot removal, sparse updates and observer delivery after publication (#43367).
- Classify Librarian failures once into immutable evidence while preserving range sizing, input admission, invalid-output veto and measured CLI capacity callbacks (#43370).
- Return explicit immutable Goal upsert commits instead of mutable result channels and physical-identity rejection; preserve revision, criterion and audit-outbox behavior. Remove the unused public `Goal_store.update_state` helper while retaining all upsert interfaces (#43374).
- Extend the OCaml refactoring audit with a stream-error diagnostic boundary candidate, three retained Agent Core ownership boundaries and explicit partial-reading scope (#43377).
- Separate pure stream-error projection from optional diagnostic file I/O; preserve full-frame redaction and terminal ordering through public HTTP streaming scenarios (#43386).
- Return Task commit receipts with their verification notification obligations, preserving late projection errors, precommit compensation and cancellation behavior (#43399).
- Isolate canonical child export selection behind a private pure typed boundary, preserving native async child authority, publication, export order and dependent artifact reads (#43411).
- Preserve native preparation-stage entry/return evidence and check that exact Task plan Tools are available in the first actual model request without redundant loading. (#43433)
- Expose opt-in durable Tool commit observations with original execution identities, isolated fiber scopes and explicit delivery failures. (#43437)
- Record each accepted early question snapshot with its original read request and refresh clock, separating usable UI state from full refresh completion. (#43440)
- The FIFO authority refusal test arms its 5 s alarm per attempt instead of once over both attempts, so slow runners no longer die by SIGALRM outside the FIFO open (#43463).
- merge-guard reads single-object GitHub endpoints without `--paginate`, so a large main tip commit no longer yields two shas and a silent exit 1; check failures now name their reason on stderr (#43464).
- Isolate declared runtime lane edit planning behind a private pure boundary, preserving locked reads, reference renames, HTTP/CLI slot order, refusal precedence and the separate typed CAS transaction (#43469).
- Represent Board contention rearm ownership with a private immutable phase, preserving exact ticket identity, delay history, scheduler locking and callback/exception order (#43479).
- Separate provider history encoding and immutable daily projection from journal traversal and diagnostics, preserving source replacement, empty-day meaning and the public history contract (#43489).
- Move the production wake-clause Codex test beside its own comment, drop an orphaned test comment, and state what the next-request forecast and the cycle failure log measure about the completion line (#43492).
- Specify Chat and Responses phase replay conformance and preserve original encrypted reasoning artifacts when only JSON object member order changes. (#43522)
- Separate durable generated-media state transitions from diagnostics and persistence while preserving completion order, failed-attempt evidence and the public accumulator interface (#43526).
- Isolate verification snapshot types, codecs and projections in one private
  module while preserving the public Store interface and acquisition effects.
  Add a persisted-request scenario covering consistent first-error handling
  across authority inspection and dashboard listing (#43553).
- Give Goal document types, codecs and schema rejection one private owner while
  preserving the public Store interface, source authority and transaction effects.
  Exercise ordered schema rejection and mutation refusal through real stored
  documents and the public validator (#43556).
- Centralize `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` credential helper wiring in `Keeper_github_identity` so MicroVM endpoints inject it only when the Keeper has a configured GitHub identity, use `Keeper_microvm_backend.scratch_guest_root` in shim prefix tests, and backfill the #43582 changelog fragment (#43602, #43582).
- Add an explicit manual macOS TUI artifact check with source identity, selected state-test execution, and a receipt that keeps runtime and visible UI verification separate. #43726
- Exercise an admitted Librarian summary when restoring tool arguments, verify empty-history source coordinates separately from omission framing, and include changed unread evidence in native Gate resume expectations (#43925).
- Drop the stray `---` frontmatter line from `changelog.d/43748.md`, which made `scripts/changelog-fragments.py check` exit 1 and would have stopped `scripts/bump-version.sh` before the next release (#43946).

## [0.58.0] - 2026-10-16

### Upgrade notes

- `skill-activation-events.jsonl` written after this version records
  `async_result_delivered` rows; earlier binaries reject the unknown kind and
  cannot decode the ledger for that trace, so do not roll back once such a row
  is written (#43179).
- `skill-activation-events.jsonl` written after this version records
  `async_action_observed` rows; earlier binaries reject the unknown kind and
  cannot decode the ledger for that trace, so do not roll back once such a row
  is written (#43188).
- Stored `keeper_msg` requests move from schema 4 to 5 and prepared execution journals from schema 1 to 2, without conversion. Old requests are refused as `unsupported keeper_msg request schema_version`; old journals cannot resume. Before replacing an existing runtime, finish or explicitly resolve its pending requests, result waits and completion delivery using that runtime. Keep the old base path and its artifacts for diagnosis; start this candidate against a fresh base path. The affected partitions are `<base-path>/.masc/keeper_msg_requests/{active,terminal,execution_journals}`. Do not clear the shared `keeper_msg_requests` root: it also retains owned-job and producer authority. No automatic deletion or in-place migration is performed. (#43201)
- Execution journals move from schema 2 to 3 without conversion. Finish or explicitly resolve pending Composition runs and completion delivery on the original runtime before replacing it. Preserve the original base path and its artifacts for diagnosis, and use a fresh base path for this candidate. Existing requests retain schema 5; old named requests without a journal do not gain logical successor authority. Affected authority remains in `<base-path>/.masc/keeper_msg_requests/{active,terminal,execution_journals,named_composition_runs,prepared_continuations}`. Do not purge the shared request root. (#43202)
- Named async calls through the internal descriptor-only compatibility adapter require a frozen turn surface. Production Keeper bundles already supply it; this does not add a runtime setting or scheduling budget. (#43202)
- Producer intents are private durable records in `<base-path>/.masc/keeper_msg_requests/named_submissions`. Preserve them with the existing request and journal partitions; missing original intent does not authorize replacement submission. This adds no migration or runtime setting. (#43205)
- Persisted nested Skill result evidence now requires `activation` and `activation_frame_sha256` fields; older nested result records without those fields are rejected as `Malformed_draft` (#43208).
- Keeper async request records now use `schema_version = 6` (`persistence_failed` carries a structured `attempted_status` object); `schema_version = 5` records are rejected without migration (#43210).
- Execution journals from earlier development candidates without the strict original Keeper-turn and replay-mode fields are rejected; missing identity is never inferred or rewritten into a fresh launch (#43216).
- Existing workspaces require an operator-selected reset before this format cut can serve approvals: archive `<base-path>/.masc/gate/pending.json` together with `pending.log.jsonl`, plus `always-allowed.json`; this removes pending approvals, retained one-shot grants and all remembered rules from active use. Preserve a full gate backup, reissue requests and explicitly approve remembered rules again. See [upgrade and rollback notes](../docs/guides/APPROVAL-RULE-STORE-UPGRADE.md); this PR does not reset runtime state. (#43361)

### Added

- Async composition completion prompts include canonical selected results and their original task, turn and run references. Larger projections retain exact result lookup coordinates; missing, inconsistent or unowned records remain explicit errors, and Keeper instructions use usable completion results directly (#42841).
- Prepared compositions can freeze a reusable Skill proposal and use the same draft digest to validate and publish its exact source bytes. Owner, package and frozen tool contracts are rechecked before publication. The generated plan codec preserves JSON values without manual TOML rewriting. (#42869)
- Added an exact frozen inline Skill compiler API with fixed parameter binding,
  collision-free node namespaces, named export mapping, and whole-child failure
  dependencies. Public draft authoring and dispatch activation integration follow
  separately; async children still require durable suspension. (#42889)
- Added durable nested composition invocation provenance and exact parent-result delivery correlation, preserving distinct child identities across readback. Skill evidence and dashboard decoders support the new typed invocation. Actual draft/executor activation wiring follows separately (#42895).
- Public inline composition drafts freeze exact child Skill recipes and mappings, revalidate them before dispatch, record attempted children through the canonical turn journal, and retain child dispositions and useful exports with the parent result. Blocked children do not activate. (#42902)
- Keeper event queues preserve the actual admission clock across duplicate intake, retention, deferral, reprioritization and fresh reads. Health and Dashboard distinguish observed residence, an empty queue and explicit missing or invalid clock evidence without deriving lifecycle decisions from duration. (#42936)
- Continue a prepared async composition with its original `resume_run_id` and
  draft digest after canonical prior-request settlement; reuse completed node
  results and occurrences under the original run, invocation and task. #42973
- Add Keeper isolated Docker job start, status and cancellation tools with

- Capture available terminal logs without process-preview truncation and retain

  writable program/CLI data outside blob-maintenance authority sources. #42989
- Bind Keeper isolated jobs to their original invocation before preparation,

- Reject changed source or command bindings before backend calls and preserve
  unknown launch intentions without creating or starting a replacement. #42995
- Added the read-only, concurrent `keeper_job_result` tool. Prepared async Compositions can retain a producer-owned wait and explicitly resume the same run to consume that original job's complete outputs. Rechecking preserves the original occurrence IDs and reuses completed siblings; generic deferrals and unknown command effects remain non-replayable. Direct pending result reads let the Keeper continue other work. Job-completion reconciliation and automatic wakes remain separate work. (#43000)
- Match the owned-job composable output schema to supported structural types and select stdout through its canonical `_blob` wrapper. (#43000)
- Preserve frozen tool contracts as canonical literal JSON so schema properties named `_blob` cannot be mistaken for artifact references during prepared-run loading. Actual execution/input references retain strict manifest validation. (#43000)
- Recover pending isolated job results on startup and the existing maintenance pulse, then deliver durable notifications with the original job, task, output references and conversation. Independent job fibers let maintenance and new jobs continue while a backend is blocked; committed results need no backend call to recover delivery. (#43009)
- Prepared Composition waits capture the exact previous worker, canonical waiting record and saved node occurrences for continuation admission. Same-job waits retain separate node identities. (#43037)
- Resume canonically ready original prepared job-result waits from server startup, the existing maintenance pulse and durable job completion hints using current TOML/meta, published Skills and exact owner/node admission, without requiring a provider turn or relaunching the job (#43109).
- Prepare and run an isolated owned-job launch inside a task composition, passing its original job ID and complete artifacts to dependent nodes while retaining the completed launch during continuation (#43129).
- Run exact inline Skill children inside prepared async parents with durable original trace, runtime, snapshot and Task provenance, actual child admission and full result scopes (#43131).
- Correlate prepared async status results with the original admitted request,

  handoffs retain separate inline/reference evidence. Correlation reaches the
  Keeper log; durable async Skill-delivery/action attribution remains pending.
  (#43157)
- `masc prerequisite-actions searxng` offers the one step that fits the
  `masc-searxng` Docker container: `searxng_docker_run` when none exists
  (writes `<base>/.masc/searxng/settings.yml` unless a file is there, pulls an
  image fixed by tag and digest, starts it with `--restart unless-stopped`,
  published on `127.0.0.1:8888` only) and `searxng_docker_start_existing` when
  one is stopped (`docker start`, nothing written). A running, paused,

- Record prepared async child result handoffs in the original session's Skill

- The setup wizard's tools checklist can choose where web search goes, in two

### Fixed

- Async composition completion notifications recover from failed queue delivery using a pre-worker durable obligation and the original canonical result. Strict queue durability, payload identity and complete consumption evidence prevent uncertain acknowledgements, conflicting results and duplicate delivery after consumption, and notification recovery never restarts the worker. The absence scan is bounded to day partitions at or after the request's submission day, so a torn write in an unrelated older partition no longer rejects a new completion notification (#42830).
- Recover recorded Ask answers on startup and the existing maintenance pulse without another operator answer. Preserve the canonical first winner, original continuation and exact once-only delivery identity. (#42955)

- Preserve recorded-versus-delivery-pending and canonical conflict receipts through the TUI HTTP and async completion paths. Unconfirmed recording remains explicit. (#42955)

- Carry owned job completion through queue identity, Keeper turn acknowledgement

- Preserve original owned-job result IDs and retained execution data when a prepared async composition releases its worker to wait. Canonical waiting attempts no longer emit a failed composition notification; completed siblings and original task/run ownership remain available for explicit resumption. (#43021)
- Retire waiting-attempt notification obligations only after exact durable request and producer proof, and recover them without rerunning workers or jobs. Keep generic and unprepared async submission behavior explicit. (#43021)
- Keep owned-job waits nonterminal in Fusion delivery projection and retain
  their delivery obligations. (#43021)
- A stale waiting continuation cannot capture a competing successor after that worker has completed; strict result readiness performs no backend operation. Automatic continuation remains separate work. (#43037)
- Preserve complete JSONL content changes as transaction failures across
  activation, approval and Board consumers; never treat them as torn tails
  or optimistic cursor conflicts. (#43053)
- Retire waiting completion obligations under the same request lock as their canonical status check, and pass locked settlement evidence to the outbox without re-entering that lock. (#43109)
- Preserve original child activation times atomically and require retained activation authority before completed or suspended child results can be reused. Keep unchanged original job waits recoverable when a successor stops before dispatch; an async submission receipt does not claim child result delivery (#43131).
- Compile prepared compositions, owned jobs and Ask answer receipts under
  the current main's exhaustive-match rules while preserving error classes,
  original job ownership, uncertain effects and durable delivery obligations.
  (#43151)

Exact physical Keeper frame, SDK coordinates, Skill, bound arguments and Task distinguish the original occurrence; uncertain broker entry cannot create a replacement worker. (#43205)
- Named Composition journals retain the original physical Keeper TurnRef and SDK invocation ordinal independently, allowing native ordinal zero in Keeper run one and client-session counter resets. (#43205)
- Keep a prepared composition's recovery marker when its first worker is lost before any result wait and the journal still contains unproven effects. Maintenance reports the unresolved node, and manual resume refuses before accepting a replacement request. Declared read-only unfinished work retains its existing manual resume. No runtime setting or durable format changes (#43206).
- Retain exact nested Skill activation receipts through execution and restoration. Child result delivery checks the original immutable admission frame, including its first activation clock, rather than accepting an invocation ID alone (#43208).
- Hold repeated automatic recovery of the same original request when activation, journal or result authority remains unavailable. Explicit resume after repair can advance its canonical owner; proven pre-effect policy refusals still settle, and uncertain parallel effects retain recovery. (#43210)
- Preserve original child occurrence IDs on proven safe retries and distinguish acceptance callback failures from later worker publication failures (#43210).
- Distinguish held original child authority from producer-proven pre-effect rejection: confirmed policy/contract rejection settles the original result, while unavailable receipts, journal ownership and uncertain accepted effects remain held. (#43210)
- Serialize canonical async request reads with the live owner's status publication so normal atomic replacement cannot interrupt a nested child submission (#43211).
- Hold automatic continuation when original draft, activation or task Skill evidence is unavailable before worker admission, so an unchanged owner cannot repeatedly rebuild the same intake after repair. (#43215)

- Search ordinary capability names as literal phrases by default, including hyphens and quoted Unicode names; require explicit `fts5` syntax for advanced search expressions. #43251
- Derive the frozen model Tool projection from canonical composition schemas so transient prepare/run Tools and their request controls do not produce false mismatch errors. (#43253)
- `network_mode = "inherit"` microVM 게스트가 호스트 DNS 서버를 글자 그대로 받아, 호스트 리졸버가 `fe80::...%en0`일 때 게스트의 모든 이름 조회가 실패하던 문제를 고친다. 이제 주소로 파싱해 존이 붙었거나 link-local, loopback, 미지정, 멀티캐스트면 게스트 부팅을 이유와 함께 거부한다. 거부는 게스트를 멈추거나 지우기 전에 한다 (#43254, #40915).
- Preserve valid reaction evidence replay after a malformed record shares its event identity, while retaining quarantine evidence (#43261).
- Resolve each Keeper's TTS voice from the active endpoint's own agent mapping before its default, and preserve those file-owned maps through setup edits (#43262).
- Keep array-of-tables field edits outside nested tables so voice setup cannot overwrite an endpoint's agent map (#43262).
- Send Gemini structured output and JSON mode through the current generateContent responseFormat.text contract (#43264).
- Keep applied Board deletions distinct from pending snapshot persistence,
  invalidate cached projections, and report pending state through MCP,
  cleanup and Dashboard receipts while retrying failed snapshots (#43267).
- Serialize approval resolution with pending and delivery publication, preserving workspace and store revalidation before delivery (#43270).
- Preserve authored text positions and native media carriers when editing a
  queued Keeper message; cancel partial edits without changing the queue (#43272).
- Dashboard conversation history reads server-issued earlier pages, retains them
  through tail refresh and live messages, and preserves failed pages for retry
  (#43274).
- A credential file the server cannot open for a moment, for example when the
  system runs out of open files, no longer leaves that credential out of the
  token index as if it did not exist. The index is built from the files it
  could read and remembers which it could not. A bearer found in it is accepted
  as before. A bearer it does not hold, while a file was unreadable, now gets a
  read failure (HTTP 503) instead of `Token mismatch`, and that index serves
  for at most 5 seconds before the files are read again. One file that stays
  unreadable affects only those bearers, not every token (#43258, #43275).
- A system I/O failure while checking a token now answers HTTP 503 instead of
  400 (#43275).
- Skip repository checkout discovery and Git for fast Keeper status reads unless `include_repository_checkouts` is explicitly selected; Dashboard detail requests retain their repository inspection. (#43277)
- Apply tool defaults to effect classification and conditional concurrency as well as execution, so an omitted argument that defaults to a mutation cannot receive read-only retry or concurrent scheduling authority. (#43288)
- Let existing-file Edit calls and Edit-only Inline Skills read a shared original concurrently when their lexical replacement targets occupy independent directories; retain write/read ordering, physical alias checks and ordinary Gate/recovery handling. (#43289)
- Page conversation history with a Keeper/file/row-bound cursor so equal or
  regressing clocks cannot skip messages; retire stale pages across server,
  dashboard and TUI while retaining independent live operation state (#43293).
- Keep raw response frames in their separate evidence field when a provider
  error omits its message; streaming and non-streaming decoders now share a
  payload-independent diagnostic instead of copying the raw frame (#43301).
- Complete a Keeper attempt on a typed empty terminal failure only after that same attempt saved tool results, while preserving the shared SDK's empty-completion rejection (#43305).
- The ask answer recovery pass no longer holds the server for over a minute
  every tick. The strict delivery check read a keeper's whole reaction ledger
  on every call, once per answered ask. It now keeps what each day file
  proved, with the file's cursor, and reads only the bytes a file gained
  since. Verdicts are unchanged. The bytes read are counted on
  `masc_telemetry_snapshot_scanned_bytes_total{store="reaction_ledger_delivery"}`
  (#43299, #43307).
- Qualify the request-depth module in the Conditional Fusion harness so the complete scenario file typechecks against the actual Fusion interface (#43311).
- Show a verified Dashboard health reading while the rest of the TUI refresh
  is still loading, without granting input or approval authority from the
  preview; stale and completed refreshes retire it (#43312).
- Start Ask and Keeper roster requests alongside the other full-refresh reads
  so slow visible-surface requests no longer postpone sending them; keep one
  request per source and verify workspace identity after every branch joins
  (#43313).
- Route Keeper attention causes to matching fleet views and clarify topbar connection and error-console information (#43315).
- Keep namespace pause controls visible and disabled while state is pending or unavailable, with a stable header footprint for operators (#43316).
- Return a stable public audit failure receipt without projecting exception text or private filesystem paths from Keeper event queue operations (#43318).
- Release the directories a prepared Edit pins by ending a switch the preparation owns instead of calling `Eio.Resource.close`, which eio_posix does not support, so a fallback or failed preparation no longer raises on macOS. (#43319)
- Read initial track/staff metadata, artist, key signatures, section labels, and parenthesized tuning when rendering supported single-part guitar and bass tablature in the TUI (#43320).
- Add deterministic regression coverage for cancellation while publishing an already durable execution-journal batch, including continued writer use and exact replay. (#43322)
- CI observer cleanup retains its command session identity and signals workers through Linux pidfds or Darwin audit tokens. Uncertain cleanup is reported explicitly while known command, timeout and cancellation statuses are preserved. (#43323)
- Full health reports waiting-inventory read failures and schedule recovery provenance, preserving observed counts while marking incomplete totals unknown. (#43326)
- A credential read failure is no longer mistaken for a token problem on the
  leftover paths: a token miss during an unreadable window is counted apart
  (`masc_auth_credential_unreadable_index_miss_total`), an unreadable
  credential reports unknown standing instead of no credential (schedule and
  lane routes answer HTTP 503 so the client retries), store contention
  answers 503 instead of 400, a live-disk read failure stays a read failure
  instead of "changed" (401), and the index rebuild reads each file once
  (#43292, #43328).
- Render `atex` code fences as alphaTex tablature, including the optional rhythm notation (#43329).
- Restore the main build: `complete_saved_tool_terminal` matched nested error patterns with a wildcard arm that failed warning 4, so it now asks `Llm_provider.Error.is_end_turn_empty_completion`, which names every constructor (#43331).
- Preserve accepted IDE observations at queue capacity while refusing new observations without blocking Keeper turns, publish refusal counts and timestamps, and retire writer ownership on teardown. (#43333)
- Pin that a continuation whose resume reports held original authority is
  not resumed again by later pulses of the same supervisor, and that a
  restarted server retries once and then holds again; document why a
  corrupt journal stays held instead of failing the run (#43268, #43334).
- Wait for Keeper detail tab selection and its rendered content in the dashboard scenario test. (#43339)
- Merge heads can now carry a merge-compile record: the four operator
  executables built from those exact inputs, settled as a commit status,
  with target freshness checked alongside. `merge-guard.sh` reports the
  verdict as advisory until convention adoption turns the refusal on.
  Heads with inputs identical to an already built SHA settle instantly by
  input identity (#43266, #43342).
- Preserve archived and offline Keeper history while distinguishing unknown names, unavailable reads and valid empty transcripts, and retire changed cached history while keeping successfully read history available during new writes. (#43343)
- Register the owned job tools and `keeper_composition_result` in the tool catalog with explicit read or write permission metadata, and add them to the matching test inventories (#43346).
- Resume Keeper history loading after a replacement read fails and preserve newer history requests and previously loaded conversations. (#43351)
- Preserve bounded private response evidence on structured output parsing failures and report their closed failure class while keeping model output and parser fragments out of public errors. (#43352)
- Attribute Keeper file observations through measured Git checkout and origin identity, including renamed clones and local linked-worktree origins, while keeping unknown or conflicting repository identity explicit. (#43354)
- Preserve typed owned-job reconciliation holds in replies so a missing created backend reports unconfirmed instead of ready, with explicit result readiness. (#43358)
- Reapproving an exact remembered Keeper rule persists its requested expiry and current-actor renewal audit. Durable resolution order and atomic application receipts keep retries, delayed writes and deletion from reviving older permissions; dashboard receipts expose the committed expiry. Pending format 12 and the canonical rule/application store explicitly refuse prior formats without rewriting retained data. (#43361)
- Preserve original backtraces from owned resource-release callbacks and close-capable files in Recovery Obligation and Reconciler while retaining callback values, cancellation and multiple cleanup failures. Automatic POSIX directory cleanup remains outside this partial repair. (#43369)
- Publish gRPC readiness only after the actual loopback socket bind, with typed listener failures isolated from HTTP readiness. (#43371)
- Order exact-lane and Keeper candidates behind a provider whose complete usage read says its quota is spent (Antigravity, Ollama, Z.AI, Kimi, OpenRouter, Muse), so a quota that resets in days no longer sends every call to it first (#43375).
- Retain accepted trajectory rows and final summaries until durable append acknowledgment, and block blind retries after uncertain writes. (#43376)
- Keep structured refusals, truncation and tool-result waits distinct from terminal JSON, including Keeper vision outcome handling. (#43384)
- Report a tool-approval-mode change as applied, with `audit_error`, when its audit record cannot be written because the audit path is blocked or unwritable, instead of failing the request with a 500. (#43392)
- Run each Antigravity one-shot call (fusion panels, exact-lane CLI slots and the vision tool) in a disposable HOME removed with the call, so the project each call creates is no longer kept per account and an `agy` start no longer opens tens of thousands of project files (#43401). The per-account homes under `.masc/official-clients/antigravity/fusion-*` are no longer used and can be deleted once the new binary runs.
- Drop the first-preparation claim of a disposable Antigravity HOME when its root is removed, so the process no longer keeps one table entry per one-shot call (follow-up to #43401, #43404).
- Declare exact OpenAI Chat model capabilities for structured output, tools and GPT-5 reasoning controls through an explicit provider binding. (#43406)
- Resolve workspace aliases once at Gate decision and retry/recovery boundaries so approvals, modes, exact rules and audits use the same owner. (#43412)

### Performance

- Composition producers can carry structured failure diagnostics once while preserving class, next move, effects, partial results and full durable evidence; opaque producer messages retain their existing presentation. (#42922)
- Share one strict reaction-evidence snapshot per Keeper across historical answered questions during recovery, retaining fresh owner-lock checks for unresolved delivery. (#42955)
- Read the known request's strict canonical Queued evidence at composition
  acceptance instead of inventorying unrelated active requests; preserve
  original-source validation, terminal precedence and run ownership CAS. (#42982)
- Collect independent TUI startup briefing, confirmation, question and Keeper roster reads in parallel while retaining workspace identity checks before and after collection. (#43296)
- Run parameterized operator summary reads in the readonly execution pool so workspace and pending-confirm disk reads do not run on the HTTP listener domain. (#43297)
- Avoid repeating a completed Keeper roster computation when another list query wins cache publication; explicit Keeper lifecycle invalidations still force a fresh read. (#43300)
- Avoid a second Agent Core checkpoint when context injectors report no updates, during ordinary tool feedback and durable terminal-result replay, while retaining the tool-result checkpoint and all reported context or message updates. (#43303)
- Carry structured Keeper list and status results directly into HTTP projections, avoiding an extra JSON encoding and parse for every successful read. (#43308)
- Prepare Keeper list and status responses, including fresh ledger projections and JSON encoding, on the existing read-only executor so the HTTP scheduler can continue serving requests. (#43309)
- The TUI sends request/response HTTP from a domain of its own, so a screen
  that redraws every pass no longer slows each reply to one step per frame:
  at 20 ms of work per frame a 1.66 MB chat history that timed out at 10 s
  arrives in 20-80 ms (#43355).
- The tool-call read index verifies a changed ledger day without copying its
  lines, and hashes the prefix once instead of twice when nothing was written
  during the scan: on a 77.6 MB day one pass put 0.1 MB on the major heap
  instead of 233.5 MB (#43372).
- A keeper turn measures only the history atoms its carried range sends,
  instead of encoding the whole history to size them: on a 20,533-message
  history one projection took 1.67 ms with no major-heap allocation instead
  of 234.3 ms and 197.7 MB (#43394).
- The tool-call read index verifies a changed ledger day on a pool domain
  instead of in a system thread of the caller's domain, so a keeper turn no
  longer makes the main scheduler wait for the runtime lock while the prefix
  is hashed: during one 77.6 MB verification a main-domain fiber woke at
  worst 1.8 ms late instead of 16.0 ms (#43407).
- Reading a whole private JSONL store sizes its buffer from the file and
  reuses one chunk, so it allocates about twice the store instead of four
  times: one read of a 34.4 MB chat event journal puts 68.8 MB on the major
  heap instead of 196.8 MB (#43413).

### Documentation

- Bundled work-intake and prior-art Skills continue known work directly, describe their concurrent reads accurately, and preserve independent lookup results on failure. Skill authoring explains selected outputs and async result recovery; a search with no match no longer implies that a problem is new. (#42855)
- Keep approval-rule reset and rollback guidance in the supported changelog upgrade section. (#43378)

### Internal

- Capture original and selected composition results through the production provider serializer and bounded artifact reader, then compare real model result recovery with recorded request bytes, usage, failures and unfinished samples. (#42914)
- Compare the two acceptance reads against the same isolated active-record
  populations, recording elapsed lookup times and returned-record counts
  independently of total preparation and external tool latency. (#42982)
- Composition dispatch scenarios decode inline result envelopes through their exact durable manifest and verify matching structured data, public owned-job scenarios validate actual producer outputs against declared schemas, and `test_every_composable_tool_has_an_output_probe` continues to guard bidirectional completeness between declared composable tools and output probes. (#43041)
- Cover the public owned-job cancellation scenario's start and recovery with its existing fixture watchdog, and retain phase and synthetic transport evidence before cancellation cleanup (#43076).
- Exercise prepared continuation output-contract rejection with a durable historical draft and an actual original job-result wait, preserving current registry-owned descriptors instead of modifying a descriptor that plan construction canonicalizes (#43099).
- Opt-in exec observations correlate actual child PIDs with captured pipe closure, exit waiting and cancellation-safe waitpid completion; owned-job scenarios emit this evidence before their existing deadlock guard cancels work, while corpus reports continue to count only exec invocations (#43102).
- Add a public job/composition scenario that resumes the original DAG only from its durable completion hint, separates backend output recovery from result consumption, and checks independent result ACK despite observer failure (#43114).
- Read the full-mode waiting and completed node results from their actual producer fields when the completion-hint recipe has no selected exports (#43114).
- Verify public nested async parents through an owned-job wait, original activation faults and fresh-supervisor recovery, retaining the original Task, runtime, Skill, occurrences and complete stdout with separate component timing receipts (#43134).
- Exercise the production nested worker after durable acceptance when original child activation becomes unreadable, then verify the same job wait and child recover through a fresh supervisor after authority restoration (#43140).
- Reuse result dependencies' canonical identities across sort comparisons and document the membership recheck after canonical terminal observation. (#43201)
- Measure reuse of an existing named Inline Skill separately from upstream task-plan preparation, retaining exact Task/Runtime/SDK/physical stdout ownership and all failed or unfinished attempts. #43246
- Add an owned-job scenario that delivers a cancelled unconfirmed launch once, confirms absence before cleanup and never repeats create/start or removes an unknown container. (#43253)
- Two matches that stopped the main build under `-w +4 -warn-error +a` now list
  every constructor: the completion outbox refuses `Waiting_for_owned_jobs`
  requests like every other non-queued status, and the owned-job log capture
  matches every `Unix.process_status` (#43276).
- Document selective Keeper status inspection and retain a sanitized live payload baseline with a separate JSON projection estimate, without claiming candidate runtime or preparation latency results. (#43278)
- Bring producer-owned Read/Write resources and default-aware tool effect/scheduling contracts onto current main, including all direct SDK consumers. The source stack had landed in an already merged parent branch. (#43288)
- Give producer-owned resource claims explicit Read or Write access, allowing shared reads to overlap while preserving overlapping write order and the existing effect, permission and replay contracts. (#43288)
- Require resource-scoped producers to declare whole-call effects independently of their resource access claims; preserve Keeper Edit/Inline effect contracts and invalidate stale read-only declarations when a scoped handler is replaced. (#43288)
- Bring the existing-file Edit entry/object resource producer and its direct/Inline execution scenarios onto current main, retaining physical alias, mutation lease and source-writer ordering. (#43289)
- Exercise Conditional Fusion escalation, skipped refinement and failed-refinement usage through the production orchestrator assembly (#43295).

### Known issues

- Test `auth_file_backed_transaction` publication 19 (`FIFO authority refuses without waiting for a writer`) is timing-sensitive: it failed once and passed on the same head in the full regression (runs 38956514813 and 38961389782). Suspected cause is a 5-second `Unix.alarm` bound; unconfirmed.
- Dispatch case 2 (PDF timeout), public lifecycle case 49 (journal race) and case 95 failed intermittently in earlier full-regression runs on the way to this cut and did not recur in the last three; cause not confirmed.

## [0.57.0] - 2026-10-16

### Upgrade notes

- `/health`: the scheduler lag percentiles and threshold counts moved under `.scheduler.lag` (#43176). Scripts that read them at the `.scheduler` top level must read `.scheduler.lag`. The repository comparison script was updated in #43199. The old key is gone and a reader gets `null` without an error, so a monitoring script that compares a lag threshold silently reads "no lag". See Breaking.
- Wiki search (`masc_wiki_search`, `keeper_wiki_search`) orders results by BM25 and searches only the title, summary, tags and body of pages whose header reads. The matching rule is unchanged, but a query no longer matches the `author` or `source` line (#43178). No configuration change.
- Local developer switches: run `scripts/opam-pin-external-deps.sh --install` once to pin `eio_posix` (#43255).
- Board MIDI playback needs `midi_soundfont` under `[tui]` in runtime.toml (#43166).

### Breaking

- `/health` scheduler lag moved from `.scheduler.<field>` to `.scheduler.lag.<field>` (#43176). A reader of the old path receives `null`, not an error. The fragments carry no Breaking marker; this entry is the release lead's disclosure, and the operator can reclassify it.

### Experimental

The user-facing features under Added below have no recorded execution evidence in their fragments, so they are Experimental until a dated run log naming the head promotes them. Guide status: `/features`, attachment opening and the MIDI soundfont setting have a guide in `docs/TUI-GUIDE.md`. Guide: none found in `docs/TUI-GUIDE.md` (read by the product owner at the cut) for `/listen`, the MIDI metadata reader, Candle pricing, exact-lane admission and the shared workspace memory log.

### Added

- The alphaTex tab renderer keeps `\title`, `\tempo` and `\ts` and draws a header line ahead of the tab (`♩=96 · 4/4 · "Riff"`, only what exists) plus a physical measure-number row above each system (#43163).
- New pure SMF reader `Masc_tui_midi`: format, tracks, names, PPQ, merged tempo map, time signatures (denominator decoded as a power of two), duration through the tempo map; SMPTE division and format 3 fail as explicit variants. User-visible from #43166 (#43164).
- Board read pane: attachments are numbered `[N]` and digit keys 1-9 open them — audio plays locally, MIDI plays via fluidsynth (new `[tui] midi_soundfont` setting, read at boot) or opens externally with the reason, Guitar Pro and other files save to the local cache and open in the default app. A status line at the pane bottom reports what happened, including a parsed MIDI summary (tracks, BPM, time signature, length) (#43166).
- Candle 지갑별 누적 반감기 차감액(`decayed_milli`), 마지막 이벤트 시각(`last_event_at`), 유통 통화량·활동 키퍼 수 요약(`supply_summary`) 및 `[shop.pricing]` 통화량 연동 동적 가격(`Fixed` | `Supply_scaled`)과 구매 시점 가격 상한 검증(`expected_price_milli` / `Price_changed`)을 더한다 (#43172).
- Add typed exact-lane admission (`Runtime.lane_requirement`, `Runtime.runtime_capability`, `Runtime.refusal`, `Runtime.admits`) and CLI slot partitioning (`Keeper_lane_cli_oneshot.partition_cli_slots`) with per-slot refusal reasons surfaced in workspace curator execution metadata and TUI lane inventory details (#43174).
- `Workspace_memory_log` and `Workspace_memory_reader` add the append-only shared workspace memory JSONL log (`Prepared` -> `Change*` -> `Committed | Aborted`) with file-locked monotonic sequence validation, mid-append truncated-tail crash recovery, and per-keeper reader cursors with context-overflow bisection and single-entry reference fallback (#43175).
- Keeper chat: `/listen` plays the newest playable attachment in the conversation — audio through the local player chain, MIDI through fluidsynth with `[tui] midi_soundfont` (same machinery as the board numbered keys). Bytes resolve from the block, the workspace media store, or a local file (#43189).
- The alphaTex score reader reads rhythm effects: a dot (`{d}`), a double
  dot (`{dd}`), a tuplet (`{tu 3}`) and a grace note (`{gr}`) change the
  latest beat's length, counted in ticks so every form lands on an integer
  (#43194).
- Lane Add-on binding inventory issues now name their failure kind: details carry a bracketed tag (`[identity-changed]`, `[absent-unconfirmed]`, `[parse]`, `[non-regular directory]`, `[unreadable]`) so publication contention reads apart from real damage without opening the store (#43212).
- `/features` opens a one-screen feature sheet — five sections, 31 rows, one sentence per feature beside the wire name that opens it (`?` keeps the key-level reference, `/help` keeps the command catalog) (#43217).
- Sheet rows draw plain text on purpose: the chat notice path renders control bytes as text, so a styled row shipped as a visible `[2m`; hierarchy lives in the diamond and the column instead of colour (#43217).
- `docs/TUI-GUIDE.md` "What can I do here" now names `/features` as the discovery one-liner (#43217).

### Changed

- `/health` `.scheduler` now nests its single-pass wake-up lag percentiles and 50ms/200ms threshold counts under `.scheduler.lag` directly from `Scheduler_lag` (#43176).
- `masc_wiki_search` and `keeper_wiki_search` list the closest page first
  inside each tier, by BM25 over the wiki's pages. Hangul is cut into
  two-character pieces, so a two-character Korean word is a term of its own.
  The matching rule is unchanged. For a page whose header reads, only the title,
  summary, tags and body are searched, so a query no longer matches the
  `author` or `source` line. A page whose header does not read is still
  searched whole (#43178).
- The Keepers detail "Current failure" section now leads a fenced empty
  assistant turn that observed no effect with a human sentence and the next
  action (message the keeper again to retry; this runtime never switches to
  another runtime automatically) instead of the
  `provider_attempt_effect_fenced` wire. A fenced turn where a tool may have
  run keeps the wire, since a retry could repeat that tool. The
  wire follows dimmed underneath as `runtime_blocker_signature`, so log
  searches keep their key, and the dashboard summary follows the same
  reading (#43195).

### Fixed

- `Candle_payout.validate_settlement` and `Candle_appraise.decide` enforce per-task Keeper eligibility consistency across all candidate tasks of the same assignee before calling the appraiser and validate `due_date` / `overdue_hours` against the confirmed `Snapshot` at CAS time (#43173).
- `Candle_shop.purchase_with_expected_price` separates the optional expected-price slippage check from `Candle_shop.purchase` so 4-argument callers compile without OCaml Warning 16 (`[unerasable-optional-argument]`) (#43186).
- Lane Add-on binding inventory reads no longer report a damaged store when a record's own rename/unlink publication races the read: `binding_inventory_with` retries an identity-changed read once and accepts a confirmed absence, so a successful concurrent write no longer flips every declaration application to `unknown` (#43209).

### Documentation

- The glossary's `Board Attachment` and `alphaTex 펜스` entries now match the TUI after #43163–#43166: attachments are numbered `[N]` and opened with digit keys (audio plays locally, MIDI through fluidsynth or, without it, only a saved path and summary; image/video open only for allow-listed extensions; file/score are saved only), and the alphaTex renderer draws a tempo/time-signature/title header and measure numbers (#43183).
- The glossary's `Candle` entry now describes `[shop.pricing]`: `fixed` (or no table) charges the base price, `supply_scaled` scales it by circulating supply per active Keeper within `min_permille`..`max_permille`, and a purchase whose effective price exceeds `expected_price_milli` is refused as `price_changed` (#43193).

### Internal

- New `Masc_tui_attachment_action` library: the kind-to-action decision (audio plays through the afplay/ffplay/mpg123/play chain, MIDI through fluidsynth with a configured soundfont and an honest external-open fallback, everything else saved to the OS-temp cache and opened locally), one playback at a time, one-line outcomes. Wired to keys in #43166 (#43165).
- `scripts/harness/perf/compare_checkpoint_history.py` merges the nested `lag`
  percentiles of a `/health` scheduler block over its top-level shape fields,
  the way `scheduler_lag_probe.sh` reads the same probe. After #43176 nested the
  percentiles under `.scheduler.lag`, the comparison died on
  `KeyError: 'samples'` and its summary table reported `None/None` for the
  scheduler column (#43199).
- `test/test_tui_command.ml`'s total `describe` matcher sweeps `Command.Listen` again: #43189 added `/listen` without updating it, so warning 8 [partial-match] became an error under `-warn-error +a` and the `Test` lane died in the compiler instead of in a case (#43203).
- `test/test_lane_addon_reconcile.ml`'s `check_application` prints the `application` JSON on failure, so the three distinct causes behind a `"unknown"` declaration application are told apart in the log instead of collapsing into `Expected/Received` (#43204).
- A test now fails when any tool in the bundle a keeper is handed advertises an input schema holding `$ref` or `$defs`, because Muse rejects the whole request when one tool carries a recursive schema (#43218).
- `eio_posix` is pinned to 1.3 plus the upstream-pending fix that retries the
  scheduler's wake-up pipe on `EINTR`, so a signal that interrupts that read no
  longer raises `Unix_error(EINTR)` out of `Eio_main.run` and ends the server
  (#43225, #43255). Run `scripts/opam-pin-external-deps.sh --install` once to
  update a local switch.

### Known issues

- Full regression run 38850227393 (head 9b6212a69409, TARGET_SUITES empty) failed. The release lead attributed it, from a quoted log reading, to an environment candidate: `Unix.ENOMEM` from `io_uring_queue_init` in `test_tui_chat_search_projection` under the parallel full run. It is a candidate, not a confirmed cause.
- Full run 38855354535 (9b6212a69409) and full run 38859872654 (ff7738ca82, the cut base) completed successfully.
- Shared workspace memory log (#43175): whether the JSONL log rotates or compacts, whether it is wired into a live path, and whether the per-Keeper reader cursor resumes after a downgrade to 0.56.0 and an upgrade back are unconfirmed. Treat it as Experimental.
- Commits merged to main after ff7738ca82 belong to v0.58 unless they fix a release-blocking defect.

## [0.56.0] - 2026-10-14

### Upgrade notes

- `MASC_CLUSTER_NAME` is no longer read. All state lives under `<base>/.masc`;
  nothing creates or reads `<base>/.masc/clusters`. A workspace that used a
  named cluster keeps that folder untouched and unread, but tool blob cleanup
  no longer counts references from it, so blobs only that folder referenced
  are removed by the next cleanups. Move or archive the folder before
  upgrading to keep them (#43017).
- The `cluster` field is removed from `/api/v1/status` and from the dashboard,
  operator snapshot, operator digest and briefing JSON. `masc_status` prints a
  `Project:` line instead of `Cluster:` (#43017).
- `.masc/root-state.json` is no longer written or read; `.masc/state.json`
  alone says a workspace is initialized. An existing `root-state.json` is
  left in place and can be deleted (#43074).
- `connectors/browser/install-host.sh` is removed. Scripts or docs that call it
  should run `masc browser-lane-setup --mode extension` instead (#42867).
- `resources/read` on `masc://wiki/log` returns only the last 64 KiB of the log,
  starting at a line boundary. A client that read the whole log through this
  resource must read `log.md` directly (#43124).
- After upgrading, every Keeper request carries a "Workspace wiki" paragraph: one line per wiki page, built at the start of the turn. Its size grows with the number of pages. Set `enabled = false` under `[wiki_contents]` in runtime.toml (or `MASC_KEEPER_WIKI_CONTENTS_ENABLED=false`) and restart to turn it off. Add the table to a live runtime.toml only after this version is running; earlier versions do not know it (#42961).

### Added

Items marked Experimental have no recorded run on a user's path yet. Each is
promoted in a later release once a live run on that path is recorded.

- Experimental: `masc web-search-setup` prints each web search provider's state and the
  search order a call would use, and writes the `[web_search]` section of
  runtime.toml when given options. It never writes an API key, and it refuses a
  SearXNG address that is not an http or https URL (#42821).
- Experimental: `masc prerequisite-actions geckodriver` and `masc prerequisite-actions firefox`
  show whether the program the browser lanes start answers `--version`, and at
  which absolute path, and offer an install action: a Homebrew step on macOS, the
  project's own page on Linux. Neither action edits `runtime.toml` (#42843).
- Experimental: `masc browser-lane-setup --mode extension` installs the browser lane for a
  workspace: the lane token, the native messaging host and its launcher, the
  Firefox native messaging manifest, and the MASC extension, which the binary
  now carries. It starts no browser. Without `--mode` it prints the lane's state
  and changes nothing (#42866).
- Experimental: `masc browser-lane-setup --mode bidi` installs the browser lane host and its
  launcher and writes the `[browser.live.bidi]` table of `runtime.toml`, so the
  MASC server starts a Firefox of its own and attaches the host to it. It writes
  no extension and no native messaging manifest. A table that is already there
  keeps its values; `--firefox`, `--profile` and `--port` change only the key
  they name. `--mode` can be given twice to connect both routes, and an option
  the chosen modes do not use is refused (#42941).
- Experimental: each Keeper turn carries the wiki table of contents: one line per wiki file (title, file, one-line summary), built from the pages at the start of the turn rather than read from `index.md`, followed by the request's route to `keeper_wiki_read` (direct, through `keeper_tool_search`, or unavailable). A wiki listing failure shows a fixed line without the IO error. Autonomous turns record the paragraph as the `wiki` layer of the dynamic-context receipt. `[wiki_contents] enabled` in runtime.toml (default `true`) turns it off (#42961).
- Experimental: `masc browser-lane-setup --mode host` installs the browser lane host and its
  launcher and nothing else: no extension, no native messaging manifest, no
  `runtime.toml`. It is for a browser the operator attaches by hand and for
  bringing an installed lane's host up to the running build (#42976).
- Experimental: `masc browser-lane-setup --mode automation` writes the geckodriver path of the
  automation lane into the `runtime.toml` the server reads. It names the
  `geckodriver` that `PATH` finds first when that file answers `--version`
  (`--geckodriver` names another); `--browser` writes `binary`, only when named.
  Keys already in the file keep their values and are edited where they are, in
  `[browser.automation]` or directly in `[browser]`. It installs no host,
  extension or manifest (#43093).
- Experimental: adding the word `rhythm` to an ```alphatex fence draws a rhythm row under the lowest string: one w/h/q/e/s letter in the first cell of each beat. A fence without it draws the same tab as before, cell for cell (#43118).
- Experimental: The install journey asks "5 · Give imp tools (optional)" after the sandbox
  step, as one checklist whose rows start marked. The browser row finds
  geckodriver and Firefox, offers the install menu for what is missing, and runs
  `masc browser-lane-setup --mode automation` before `masc setup` starts the
  server. The GitHub row offers the login `gh` holds on this computer (account,
  scopes and token source are shown first) and, once `masc setup` has created
  imp, passes the token to `masc keeper-github set-token --keeper imp` on
  standard input; without a login it runs the one-time code login. Nothing is
  installed or written until the list is confirmed, unmarking every row skips
  the step, and quick setup only prints the rows with their commands (#43119).
- Experimental: Keeper compositions can declare typed output exports and preserve complete node inputs/results in a durable execution artifact. TOML and structured JSON plans expose the existing independent-branch failure policy and retain both contracts when parameters are bound (#43137).
- Experimental: Keepers can prepare and inspect a task-specific read-only composition without publishing a shared Skill, then run the exact Keeper-bound draft inline or asynchronously. Drafts bind inputs, mode and frozen tool contracts, and record the source invocation before dispatch (#43137).
- Experimental: Independent named inline Skill compositions can overlap when every leaf permits concurrent reads. Each invocation keeps its own causal history, run identity, observations and activation evidence while the owning turn continues to collect all completions (#43137).
- Experimental: The install journey's "5 · Give imp tools" checklist gains two rows that
  connect a Firefox: BiDi (MASC starts a Firefox of its own on a local debugging
  port, with a notice that the port has no authentication) and the MASC add-on
  (through your everyday Firefox, with a notice that Firefox removes the add-on
  when it restarts). Both start unmarked and are shown only when Firefox was
  found. The chosen routes go to one `masc browser-lane-setup` call, which plans
  all of them before writing any, and run before `masc setup` starts the server.
  Quick setup marks each row `[x]` or `[ ]` in its list and runs nothing (#43138).
- Experimental: Add `scripts/migrate-lane-addon-bindings.py`, which classifies lane add-on binding records written by v0.48.0 or earlier using the container's own rules, and can move the records that are safe to move out of the read path (#43139).
  - Usage: `python3 scripts/migrate-lane-addon-bindings.py --base-path <masc base path> [--write-out <archive dir>]`. The default run is classify-only and changes nothing; it prints one line per record and the before/after counts. `--write-out DIR` (run with the server stopped) additionally archives every detached legacy record byte-identically to `DIR/<name>.json.legacy` (hash-verified) and renames the store file to `<name>.json.migrated`, which the store skips because `read_bindings` reads only files ending in `.json`. Records that are not detached are never moved or rewritten: repairing one means adding top-level `visibility` and `source_access`, which is an authority decision, and the tool reports those instead.
- Experimental: The install journey's "5 · Give imp tools" checklist gains a web search
  check, marked from the start. Confirmed, it runs `masc web-search-setup` with
  only the workspace, which writes nothing: it shows which providers have a key
  and which variable to export for one that has none. It runs in the
  environment the server `masc setup` starts gets, without `MASC_BASE_PATH` and
  `MASC_CONFIG_DIR`. A refused or unstartable command says how to look again
  and does not end the journey. Quick setup lists the row and runs nothing
  (#43145).
- Experimental: `masc_web_search` gains a `zai` provider over z.ai's Web Search MCP server
  (GLM Coding Plan). It reads `ZAI_API_KEY`, the variable the `glm-coding`
  model provider already uses, and joins the chain only when named in
  `provider`, `provider_order` or `fallbacks`: a key that is present on every
  GLM install is not asking for the plan's search allowance to be spent. A
  search is three requests, each under `MASC_WEB_SEARCH_TIMEOUT_SEC`
  (#43162).

### Changed

- The "no web search provider is configured" failure names every credential
  variable and points to `masc web-search-setup`. Provider selection and the six
  provider fetchers read their credentials through one table,
  `Web_search_provider` (#42821).
- The TUI no longer shows "persistence failure history unavailable; provider completeness and liveness unknown" as a `CHILD HEALTH` line on every Child content read. The value never changed, so it read as an alarm and hid real diagnostics. A short caveat that failure history only lives as long as the collector is attached only when a real failure is shown (#42857).
- The lane token rule (at least 16 visible ASCII characters, whitespace around
  it trimmed) is one function, `Browser_lane.Lane_token.of_text`, read by the
  browser host, the server's lane routes and `masc browser-lane-setup`. The
  server now also refuses a token with a space, control or non-ASCII character
  inside, which the host never accepted (#42866).
- `scripts/install-local-build.sh` checks each registered browser lane host after
  `masc browser-lane-setup` has run: the registration must still name the same
  launcher and the host beside it must be the one just installed. A workspace
  that fails either check, or whose refresh fails, is named on stderr and left
  as it was; the other workspaces are still refreshed and the script exits with
  status 1 (#42867).
- Where MASC starts the Firefox (a table exists in `runtime.toml`), the sentence
  that tells an operator to install the lane names `--mode bidi`, not
  `--mode extension` (#42941).
- `scripts/install-local-build.sh` also refreshes the host of the workspace it
  works with when masc's own lookup resolved it, its lane is installed and no
  manifest covers it, which is how a lane set up with `--mode bidi` or
  `--mode host` is found. A lane that has an extension and no manifest there is
  named on stderr and left as it is (#42976).
- Where the operator starts the Firefox by hand (no `[browser.live.bidi]` table),
  the sentence that tells them to install the lane names `--mode host`, which
  writes no extension and no `runtime.toml`, instead of `--mode extension`
  (#42976).
- `Dated_jsonl.Store` lists every store under one root, `<base>/.masc`: the
  `Base` and `Cluster` groups merge into `Root`, `cluster_root` becomes `root`
  (made by `root_of_base_path` or `root_of_masc_dir`), and `base` and `cluster`
  become `at`. `reaction_ledger`, `decision_audit`, `locations_on_disk` and
  `Dated_jsonl.prune_listed_stores` take that root alone (#43022).
- `Workspace.dated_store_cluster_root` is renamed `dated_store_root`, and
  `Server_runtime_startup_maintenance.prune_shared_jsonl_stores` takes
  `~masc_root` without `~base_path` (#43022).
- `Telemetry_unified.read_unified`, `read_unified_result` and `summary_json`
  take `~masc_root` without `~base_path`, as do the source-meta store
  helpers. `Keeper_wire_capture.capture_request`, `capture_response` and
  `capture_rejected_reasoning` take `~base_path` without `~masc_root` and
  write under `<base_path>/.masc`, and
  `Server_runtime_startup_maintenance.prune_jsonl_at_resolved_window` takes
  `~base_path` alone (#43047).
- The Discord connector descriptor no longer carries `names_path` and `names`, which were always `""` and `null`; its status and descriptor views are rendered from one reading instead of the descriptor reading the status JSON back by key (#43080).
- The MCP `initialize` instructions no longer tell clients to set
  `MASC_CLUSTER_NAME`, and the `masc_status` tool description no longer
  mentions cluster info (#43086).
- `--mode automation` says when a `geckodriver` or `binary` value it keeps is not
  an executable file now (a brew upgrade or a removed install). The program is
  looked for and never started. The value is left as it is and the note names the
  flag that changes it (#43093).
- `Browser_runtime_dependencies.locate` answers whether a program is there
  without starting it; `probe` runs what it finds (#43093).
- `--mode bidi` and `--mode automation` share one guard that refuses to edit a
  `runtime.toml` where a table is spelled with dotted keys or inline, and one
  commit step that compares the file's revision again just before writing. When
  both modes are given, the second table is planned again after the first is
  written, without running Firefox or geckodriver a second time. A `--firefox` or
  `--geckodriver` value with a space around it is refused instead of being
  trimmed in the check and written untrimmed (#43093).
- A Keeper execution receipt whose `operator_disposition_reason` is not one the receipt writer produces is treated as damaged: the trust snapshot no longer relays its disposition and shows its own verdict instead (#43116).
- The first conversation is step 6 of the install journey (#43119).
- `execute_prerequisite` in the setup helper reads geckodriver and Firefox
  receipts instead of refusing them as an unreadable result (#43119).
- `resources/read` on `masc://wiki/log` returns the log's tail — the last 64 KiB, starting at a line boundary — instead of the whole file, so an append-only log's read no longer grows with the file. The listing still reports the whole-file size (#43124).
- `masc_wiki_lint` is no longer experimental: the tool description, `docs/guides/wiki-lint.md` and the glossary now state the seven finding kinds and the response fields as stable, while a later RFC step may still add a kind (`revision_log_gap`). A live call on 2026-10-14 matched the hand-counted values on all five items (#43130).
- The boot-time message counter repair scans the filed messages before it
  takes the state lock and holds the lock only to read and write the
  counter, so numbering a message at boot no longer waits for the scan
  (#43132).
- Rows of the "5 · Give imp tools" checklist no longer all start marked: each
  row says whether it does, and the BiDi and add-on rows do not (#43138).
- A geckodriver or Firefox whose catalog cannot be read no longer hides the
  rows that do not need it: the Firefox routes need Firefox only (#43138).
- The note that a running workspace server must be restarted is printed only
  for the routes that write a `runtime.toml` table (automation and BiDi). The
  add-on route writes none (#43138).
- `masc_wiki_lint` now reads `log.md` as well: it reports a new `revision_log_gap` finding when the log records an `r<N>` a page never reached (with `log_revision` and `page_revision`), and two counts of its own, `log_unknown_action` and `log_unreadable_line`, for log lines whose action word it does not know and lines it cannot read. The log parser is pure and never fails; the finding kind enum, the guide and the RFC table move with it (#43149).
- `masc_wiki_lint` reports a new `revision_log_hole` finding when `log.md` skips an `r<N>` below the highest revision it records for a page; `missing` carries the skipped number. A page's lines run `r1`, `r2`, … with no skips, so the missing value is a line that reached the page and never reached the log — what an `append_log` that failed leaves. A write in flight only leaves the top of the column empty, so that is not a hole. The check refuses rather than guesses twice: it reports no hole at all when the log has any dropped line, and it starts the column at the lowest revision the log records for the page (#43155).
- `masc_wiki_lint` adds `revision_log_hole_suppressed` (boolean) to its response so callers can distinguish "no revision holes found" from "the `revision_log_hole` check was turned off because `log.md` has at least one unknown action or unreadable line" (#43169).
- Add `gemini-4-argon` to the embedded model catalog (`packages/agent_core/models.toml`) and bind the current Antigravity CLI models (`antigravity-gemini-4-argon-{high,medium,low}`, `antigravity-claude-opus-5-5-{high,medium,low}`, `antigravity-claude-sonnet-5-5-{high,medium,low}`) in `config/runtime.toml` (#43120).

### Removed

- `connectors/browser/install-host.sh` is gone. `masc browser-lane-setup --mode
  extension` does what it did and also writes the extension, so no source
  checkout or download is needed. `scripts/install-local-build.sh` refreshes
  registered browser lane hosts through that command (#42867).
- `Env_config_core.cluster_name` and `cluster_name_opt`,
  `Backend_types.config.cluster_name`, `Workspace_utils.masc_root_dir_from`
  and `Common.clusters_dir_from_base_path` (#43017).
- Tool blob maintenance no longer sweeps `.masc/clusters`: the
  `Cluster_workspace_rejected` error and the `skipped_cluster_files` report
  field, also in the deployment preflight output, are gone (#43017).
- `Workspace.masc_root_dir` (use `Workspace.masc_dir`),
  `Workspace.masc_dir_from_base_path` (use `Common.masc_dir_from_base_path`),
  `Workspace.keepers_runtime_dir_for_base_path` (use
  `Common.keepers_runtime_dir_of_base`) and `Workspace.root_key_of_path` (use
  `Workspace.key_of_path`). Each gave the same value as the name it is
  replaced by (#43031).
- `Workspace.ensure_workspace_bootstrap` (use `Workspace.init`),
  `Workspace.root_is_initialized` (use `Workspace.is_initialized`),
  `Workspace.root_state_path`, and `Workspace.read_json_root`,
  `write_json_root` and `path_exists_root` (use `read_json`, `write_json` and
  `path_exists`) (#43074).
- `GET /api/v1/mentions/<agent>` and the `Mention_inbox` module are removed: they read `.masc/mention_inbox.jsonl`, which no code writes, so the route could only return an empty list. The dashboard's mention inbox is built from messages and is unchanged (#43103).

### Fixed

- Listing the wiki (`resources/list`) no longer reads every wiki page file and
  the whole `log.md` on each call. A page now costs a stat and at most a
  bounded header prefix (8192 bytes; a page larger than that whose header does
  not read from the prefix falls back to the whole file), and the log is sized
  by stat, so the reported sizes are unchanged (#42967).
- Narrowing the chat pane while reading a held turn excerpt (scrolled-up polled speech) re-lays the excerpt's inline margin out at the pane's current badge column instead of keeping the margin laid out for the pane width the pin was made at; the held line stays where it was, and widening still keeps the excerpt's rows byte-identical (#43068).
- The boot-time repair of a message counter that fell behind the filed
  messages now runs: it lived only in `ensure_workspace_bootstrap`, which
  the server never called, and now runs in `Workspace.init` (#43074).
- `Workspace.init` writes the declared default workspace state, so a fresh
  workspace with messages already filed resumes the counter past them
